- audit every warning, error, cancellation, false positive, and false negative in the ten default-branch runs named by issue #1012
- split the timed-out Intel macOS core suite into three filter-aware cargo-nextest slices while retaining a separate specification lane and a 25-minute job limit

Fixes https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/932

## Summary

- declare the language → `link-foundation/box` image mapping and the traditional init commands as data in `data/meta/box-language-projects.lino`, read by Rust, by both shell scripts and by the CI-matrix invariant test
- generate the project corpus out of the solver itself — the program from English, Russian, Hindi and Chinese prompts, the init script from the contract's own README steps — and build and run it inside the matching image
- add a `box-language-projects` CI matrix leg, one runner per language, gated like the other slow legs
- expose the same check from `cargo test`, skipping gracefully when Docker is unavailable
- fix the routing defect the corpus exposed: install guides that name project creation were answered by the software-project planner

This is the part of PR #119 that was never delivered. The maintainer asked to "*test each software project of a specific language inside such version of link foundation box docker image, that matches the language*" and to "*use traditional commands to init repositories for each language*"; no CI leg has ever done that.

## Reproduction

Building the corpus surfaced a dispatch bug. Asking for the Go installation guide as a shell script — the exact prompt the generator issues — answered with a software-project *plan*:

```
  left: "software_project_plan"
 right: "installation_conversion"
test installation_conversion::go_module_install_guide_converts_to_a_script ... FAILED
```

The complete pre-fix output is preserved in `docs/case-studies/issue-932/raw-data/repro-before.log`, captured by reverting the promotion gate this PR adds.

`data/seed/handler-precedence.lino` already ranks `installation_conversion` (42) ahead of `software_project` (46), but `MethodRegistry::ordered_method_names_for_relevants` hoists *any* method named by a `handler:<name>` relevant ahead of the whole precedence table. The promotion array emitted `handler:software_project` and `handler:write_script` and never `handler:installation_conversion`, so a guide whose steps say "create the project" and "build the project" matched the promoted cues and the declared precedence never applied. The array also moved to `src/intent_formalization/prompt_relevants.rs`: the parent module was at 897 of its reviewed 900-line ceiling.

## Design

`data/meta/box-language-projects.lino` is the single contract — registry, namespace, image tag, project directory, expected output, the four prompt locales, and one record per language carrying its image, program file, code fence, optional shell prelude, whether the init needs network, and the ordered traditional init steps.

`scripts/generate-box-language-corpus.sh` asks the solver for the program once per locale and refuses to continue unless the four answers are byte-identical, rebuilds the installation guide from the contract's init steps, asks the solver to convert that guide into a shell script, and asserts every declared command survives the conversion. `scripts/verify-box-language-projects.sh` streams the corpus into `docker run` as a `tar` stream (bind mounts would land root-owned host files or mismatch the container's `box` uid) and runs `scripts/run-box-language-project.sh` inside the image, which fails unless the init script exits zero, the project directory exists and the program prints `Hello, world!`. Legs whose init needs no network run with `--network none`.

`data/meta/box-image-survey.lino` records the Docker Hub survey: six per-language variants exist under `konard` (`box-rust`, `box-python`, `box-js`, `box-go`, `box-java`, `box-ruby`), all publishing `2.4.0`, which is therefore the pinned tag — `latest` was rejected because the check must not change meaning between two runs of the same commit. `konard/box-c`, `box-cpp`, `box-csharp` and `box-dotnet` do not exist, so C, C++ and C# are recorded as deferred records naming the full `konard/box` image they wait for, instead of being silently dropped. `every_matrix_image_was_actually_found_on_the_registry` fails if the matrix ever names an image the survey did not find.

The images are 4.21–7.81 GB, so no single runner holds several of them next to a cargo build. That is why the CI leg is a matrix — one image per runner — and why it frees runner disk first.

## Verification

Every language was built and run by hand inside its image before CI was trusted; the logs are `docs/case-studies/issue-932/raw-data/verify-<language>.log`:

```
ok: rust project built and printed Hello, world! inside konard/box-rust:2.4.0
ok: python project built and printed Hello, world! inside konard/box-python:2.4.0
ok: javascript project built and printed Hello, world! inside konard/box-js:2.4.0
ok: typescript project built and printed Hello, world! inside konard/box-js:2.4.0
ok: go project built and printed Hello, world! inside konard/box-go:2.4.0
ok: java project built and printed Hello, world! inside konard/box-java:2.4.0
ok: ruby project built and printed Hello, world! inside konard/box-ruby:2.4.0
```

- `cargo test --test unit` — 2745 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo test --test unit -- ci_cd::issue_999 issue_673_self_ast_census issue_918 ci_cd::issue_932 issue_932 installation_conversion` — 49 passed, re-run after merging `main`
- `cargo test --doc`, `cargo check --examples --all-features`
- `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --lib --bins --tests --all-features` — clean
- `shellcheck` (via `koalaman/shellcheck:stable`) on all four new and edited scripts — clean

A repository-wide parallel run also produced 18 integration failures, all `Os { code: 11, kind: WouldBlock }` while opening sockets on a loaded 6-core box. All 24 of those tests pass when rerun with `--test-threads=2` (`ci-logs/integration-rerun.log`), so they are runner resource exhaustion, not regressions. Fresh GitHub Actions at the final pushed SHA provide the clean sharded verification.

This is a CI and container change, not visual UI work, so before/after screenshots and visual regression tests do not apply.

## Self-hosting and evidence

The real Formal AI Agent CLI authored one of the five smallest implementation leaves: the box image survey. Session `ses_fffb7e760ffeebqPgLR1KV1DK5`, the server log, the CLI log, the decomposition and the byte-identical artifact are preserved under `docs/case-studies/issue-932/self-hosting-authorship/`, and `tests/unit/issue_932_self_authoring.rs` fails if the committed `data/meta/box-image-survey.lino` ever stops matching the captured artifact. `experiments/issue_932_self_authoring/run.sh` reproduces the session.

The issue case study, requirement matrix (R932-1 … R932-13), image survey and raw GitHub evidence are under `docs/case-studies/issue-932/` and `docs/requirements/issue-0932-box-language-projects.md`.

## Summary

- Mine reusable operation sequences from three real recursive-core event logs with the existing held-out algorithm-discovery pipeline.
- Keep every proposal inert until canonical gates pass and a human explicitly runs `--apply --confirm`; promoted records remain data and never become executable handlers.
- Load the adopted seed into the method registry, retain rejected proposals with reasons, and replay the complete workflow in CI.
- Bound free-form evidence sampling so a large log cannot make repository validation exceed CI's job budget, while retaining exact metadata plus head and tail evidence.

## Root cause

Algorithm discovery could validate inert candidates, and promotion could replay trusted gates and materialize approved changes, but there was no bridge from real `EventLog` traces through those stages into the method registry. The registry also represented only compiled handlers, so it had no safe data-only representation for learned methods.

## Reproduction and verification

The new minimal regression test initially failed to compile because the event-log learning module and learned-method registry surface did not exist. It now proves that:

1. A repeated method is abstracted from two training logs and survives a held-out benchmark.
2. Discovery alone cannot change the registry.
3. Promotion requires canonical gate evidence plus explicit confirmation.
4. The adopted record is visible in the registry without becoming a dispatchable handler.
5. Failed candidates remain durable with suite-specific rejection reasons.
6. Localized event payloads in every registered language learn the same stable control-flow method.

Validated locally with:

## Summary

Fixes #1001 — the released container image `ghcr.io/link-assistant/formal-ai` is private, so anonymous `docker pull` fails with `unauthorized`, and nothing in the release pipeline ever noticed.

**Root cause (verified):** a container package created by a `GITHUB_TOKEN` push starts private, and it does not inherit the visibility of the repository it is linked to — only its access permissions. `.github/workflows/release.yml` pushed and moved on, so every release since the first push shipped an image no anonymous consumer could fetch, with a green build.

Live probe re-run while preparing this PR (no credentials):

```
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' \
    "https://ghcr.io/token?service=ghcr.io&scope=repository:link-assistant/formal-ai:pull"
401
```

401 = the package exists and is **private** (403 would mean absent, 200 public).

## Changes

- **`scripts/verify-ghcr-visibility.sh`** (new) — credential-free probe of GHCR's anonymous token endpoint. `200` passes; `401` fails with the manual remedy; `403` fails as "the push likely never happened"; transport errors and 5xx are retried (3 attempts, configurable) and then reported as *transient*, never as "private". The issued pull token is never printed, and the probe deliberately sends no credentials — authenticating would make a private package answer 200 and recreate exactly the false negative being closed. Following the issue #977 convention, one script is shared by both release paths.
- **`.github/workflows/release.yml`** — the verification step runs immediately after the GHCR push in **both** `auto-release` and `manual-release`, under the same `if:` condition as the push it verifies.
- **`README.md`** — how to tell a private package from a missing one, and the two workarounds (`docker login ghcr.io` with `read:packages`, or `cargo install formal-ai --locked`) until the package is made public.
- **`tests/unit/ci-cd/issue_1001.rs`** (new, 10 tests) — one test per requirement plus workflow-level whole-task coverage.

## Reproduction and verification

Reproduction is the `401` above; the automated test reproduces it hermetically with a fake `curl` on `PATH` (the `scripts/install-node-dependencies.sh` sandbox pattern from issue #796), so no network is touched:

```
$ cargo test --test unit --all-features ci_cd::issue_1001
running 10 tests ... test result: ok. 10 passed; 0 failed
```

Covered: public passes (and no retry, and no token in the log); private fails with `PRIVATE` + "Change visibility"; absent fails with `DENIED` and is *not* called private; 503 is retried 3× and reported as transient; an unexpected status fails loudly instead of passing by default; an unset `GHCR_IMAGE` is not silent success; the probe scope strips the `ghcr.io/` host and any `:tag` / `@digest`; the script contains no credential plumbing; both release jobs call the script after the push with the push's own condition; the script parses under `bash -n`.

Every assertion fails against the pre-fix pipeline. Local CI (`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --lib --bins --tests --all-features`, full `ci_cd` suite — 193 tests) is green.

## What this PR cannot do

- **Making the package public is manual.** Package visibility is not settable through the REST API ([community discussion #33310](https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/33310)): package page → *Package settings* → *Danger Zone* → *Change visibility* → *Public*. **@konard**, this one-off step is still needed — until it is done, the new gate will (correctly) fail the next release.
- **The Docker Hub mirror is a repository-variable setting.** `scripts/configure-dockerhub-publishing.sh` already publishes a mirror whenever `DOCKERHUB_IMAGE` is set; setting that variable is a repository-settings action, not a code change.
title: fix(ci): fail the release when the GHCR image is not anonymously pullable

## Summary

- identify the repeated Intel macOS failure as a 35-minute capacity boundary, then split that lane into complementary `core` and `specification` shards without raising its timeout or dropping coverage
- move concurrency from mixed workflows to individual jobs, retaining cancellation for superseded reads while placing every material repository writer in a non-lossy `queue: max` scope
- eliminate current warning debt: use the supported Pages timeout, classify intentional exemptions/reports as notices, and bring all five flagged files below their warning thresholds
- add the missing CodeQL, dependency-review, and live-link gates; repair five stale documentation links and keep Wayback diagnostic-only so archived copies cannot make dead live links pass
- enable the repository's Dependency Graph prerequisite after the first remote Dependency Review run exposed that settings-level gap; SBOM export and base/head comparison now succeed
- preserve the complete issue/PR/run/template investigation, root-cause analysis, timeline, alternatives, source research, and verification logs in a SHA-256-manifested evidence archive
- strengthen the split-seed regression after the first full remote lint run correctly required language-matrix coverage; all four moved intents are now checked for every registered locale and every runtime loader
- fix a fresh link-gate finding: replace a repeatedly unavailable reference with live university course material, and prevent the Wayback helper from misreporting Lychee's successful redirects as broken links

## Root causes

The latest default-branch pipeline had no failed or hanging test. Its Intel macOS job was still producing passing specification results when GitHub killed it at the unchanged 35-minute limit. The last successful instance already took 28m37s, so cold build time plus the growing monolithic suite had exhausted the remaining margin.

The wider audit also found a cancellation-scope defect: read checks and write jobs shared workflow-level concurrency. A newer run could interrupt an active writer, and GitHub's default one-pending-run behavior could replace an older queued writer. Job-level concurrency now matches side-effect boundaries.

A fresh link run found one real 502 and 18 healthy redirects. The copied template helper parsed every Markdown bullet across both sections and announced 19 broken URLs. It now parses only Lychee's error section (with a compatibility fallback), covered by a red/green Node regression; the unavailable source was replaced rather than ignored or excused by its archive.

The complete root-cause analysis and all nine issue requirements are mapped in the [durable evidence report](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/issue-999-31976d2c6ce9/dev/log/issues/999/pulls/1000/README.md).

- issue #999 regressions: 6/6

- self-AST census: 8/8; browser suite: 53/53
- Clippy with warnings denied, examples, normal/docs.rs rustdoc, formatting, actionlint 1.7.12, ShellCheck, changelog reconstruction, fragment mapping, file-size enforcement, diff check, and repository secret scan: passed

Full logs are in the evidence report and the [readable case study](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/issue-999-31976d2c6ce9/docs/case-studies/issue-999/README.md).

No visual UI behavior changed, so screenshots do not apply.

## Upstream reports

- corrected the Rust template's obsolete concurrency conclusion in [issue 113](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/113#issuecomment-5257178147)
- reported the shared archived-link false negative with reproductions, workarounds, and code fixes in [Rust #125](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/125), [JavaScript #127](https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/127), and [Python #54](https://github.com/link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/54)

## Summary

- make the macOS packaging retry log genuinely unique under BSD `mktemp`, and align the proxy-log assertion with the product's canonical path
- centralize BSD/util-linux `script(1)` PTY launch syntax, guard empty Bash arrays under stock macOS Bash 3.2, and restore a full `macos-15-intel` test leg
- make the shared runner-disk bootstrap use POSIX `df -Pk`, after the first fresh macOS job exposed its GNU-only `--output=avail` flag
- wait for the fake interactive client before writing and defer PTY EOF until command exit, after macOS exposed both lifecycle races
- add per-requirement and whole-task regressions, issue/PR case studies, and real Formal AI / Agent CLI authorship evidence

## Root causes

The Linux-only test matrix hid four independent platform assumptions: a suffix after `mktemp`'s placeholder, a raw-vs-canonical path comparison, util-linux-only PTY flags, and an unguarded empty-array expansion under Bash 3.2 nounset semantics. The first new macOS job also exposed GNU-only `df --output=avail` in its pre-test disk cleanup; that helper now uses the POSIX `df -Pk` columns. Two later jobs exposed both halves of an interactive-test race: BSD `script` could deliver terminal EOF before the fake client started reading, and closing its input immediately after a write could translate that close into EOT ahead of the buffered line. The PTY helper now waits for a line-ending-independent readiness marker, sends input, and retains stdin until the command exits.

## Tests

- `cargo test --test issue_961_macos_portability -- --nocapture`
- `cargo test --test issue_757_session_files -- --nocapture`
- `cargo test --test unit macos_package_retry -- --nocapture`
- `cargo test --test integration pty:: -- --nocapture`
- both affected PTY integration tests
- `cargo test --workspace --all-features --no-fail-fast --verbose`
- formatting, Clippy, example checking, and repository integrity scripts

The tests-first issue contract failed all five original assertions before the implementation. After the first pushed macOS job failed before Cargo, two additional tests reproduced its BSD `df` error. The next jobs exposed the PTY readiness and early-EOF races; each received a failing regression before its repair. The complete issue contract is now 12/12 and the shared PTY helper suite is 4/4. The original macOS audit's six failing cases and the post-fix evidence are documented in the case study.

Final SHA `9fa69dfc` passed the complete [CI/CD Pipeline](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/runs/31396066284), including `Test (ubuntu-latest)` and `Test (macos-15-intel)`. ## Summary

- preserve explicit tool failure metadata across OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, and Responses inputs
- separate observed attempts from successful planner steps, recover one rejected write with read + bounded retry, preserve the primary write when an auxiliary plan write fails, and stop honestly on repeated or verification failures
- require successful verification output to match the requested bytes before reporting completion
- seed mismatch/unverified responses in all five supported languages and refresh generated closure/self-AST evidence

Closes #905.

## Reproduction and root cause

The reported prompt, `Create a file hello.txt containing exactly: Hello World`, reproduced three defects: the shorter equal-start marker left `exactly:` in the payload; provider error metadata was discarded while every tool result counted as completed; and the general planner emitted success based on call counts without checking result status or output.

The pre-fix focused suite retained in `docs/case-studies/issue-905/test-evidence/regression-red.log` fails 6 of 7 assertions. Both original Agent CLI provider traces and authenticated issue/PR snapshots are retained in the case study. This is a protocol/state bug, so no visual screenshot applies.

## Relationship to `main`

While this branch was open, `main` landed its own fixes for the three defects named in the original issue text: `strip_clause_lead` in `src/agentic_coding/general_planner.rs` (control-phrase parsing) and `ShellEnvelope`/`failed_verification` in `src/agentic_coding/tool_result.rs` (exit-code-aware failure reporting). Those implementations are kept as-is by this merge; the branch's earlier, narrower versions were dropped.

What remains unique to this pull request is the requirement added by the qwen trace in the issue comment — `is_error: true` tool results were being discarded entirely, so the plan advanced over a step that never ran:

- `ChatMessage::is_error` on the shared protocol type, populated from Anthropic `tool_result.is_error`, Responses `is_error`/`isError`/failed `status`, and the OpenAI-compatible `is_error`/`isError` fields
- `Progress` recording observed attempts separately from satisfied steps, so a rejected call cannot count as progress
- the two-turn `read_file` → `write_file` recovery the issue comment asked for, bounded per target path
- content-match verification: literal completion compares transport-normalized command output against the request-derived payload
- `general_execution.rs`, the plan's execution state machine, split out of the planner

## Verification

Latest run, on `06d5a9e2`, which merges `origin/main` (`52ef42e7`, v0.333.0) into the branch:

- `cargo test --test unit` — 2574 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored

- `cargo fmt --check`; `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`

- `check-file-size`, `check-associative-terminology`, `check-hardcoded-language`, `check-disk-usage-policy`, `check-worker-line-budget`, `check-changelog-fragment` — all passed
- CI on the merged head `06d5a9e2`: CI/CD Pipeline, Coverage, Write-Effect Ladder, Task Ladder, Agentic CLI Matrix, Agent CLI E2E, External Benchmarks, Desktop Release — all eight green

Generated artifacts (self-AST census, planner fixtures, total-closure shards) were regenerated from the merged sources, so they remain pure functions of `src/**` and `data/seed/**`.

Regression coverage includes the exact prompt, 20 parsing variants, Qwen-style explicit errors, Codex-style nonzero exits, bounded write recovery, wrong/matching verification evidence, requested failure vocabulary, and Anthropic/Responses parity. Acceptance traceability is in `docs/case-studies/issue-905/requirements.md`.

## Merge with `main` (v0.333.0)

`main` advanced repeatedly while this branch was open, and each time the pull request went conflicted the conflicts were confined to *generated* artifacts — `data/meta/self-ast/index.lino` and the `data/seed/closure-generated-*.lino` shards. None was ever resolved by hand: `main`'s side was taken and then both artifact families were regenerated from the merged sources (`cargo run --example regenerate_self_ast_census`, `python3 scripts/close-total.py`), so the committed bytes remain exactly what the generators produce. No source file has conflicted at any point.

The final merge (`06d5a9e2`, bringing in `52ef42e7` / v0.333.0) had a single conflict, in `data/meta/self-ast/index.lino`, resolved the same way. The branch is now `MERGEABLE` against `main`.

## The completion claim is now seeded, not English in Rust

The sentence this issue quotes as the false report — `Completed the general change request for … and verified it with …` — was the last outcome of the general-change state machine still typed into `src/` as an English literal, while every failure path (`general_plan_unverified`, `general_plan_verification_mismatch`, `general_plan_repository_planned`) already resolved through the seed. That contradicted the repository's meanings ↔ naturalization rule: a Russian or Chinese request that *succeeded* was answered in English, while the same request that *failed* was answered in its own language.

`general_plan_completed` is now a seeded intent in all five supported languages, rendered through `localized_response`. The English text is byte-identical, so every existing assertion is unchanged; `scripts/hardcoded-language-allowlist.txt` loses exactly one entry, and the five-language response test now covers the completion claim alongside the two failure intents.

## Same-task self-application

Formal AI served the `formal-ai` model to the external Agent CLI in session `ses_034e9dafeffe7nxeTkFhmHLmZN`, which authored and read back the canonical tool-result evidence invariant. That is 1 of 5 reviewed smallest leaves (20%). Session `ses_03474fd81ffeMofsJrUWdYDEEd` refreshed the planner-derived self-healing fixture through the same real client/server path. Replay harnesses and byte-identical artifacts are retained under `experiments/issue_905_*` and `docs/case-studies/issue-905/`.

An earlier whole-issue attempt selected an unsupported hosted fallback and received HTTP 401 before Formal AI executed. It is retained as failed infrastructure evidence and is not counted as authorship; echoed authorization headers are redacted.


## Write-effect ladder regression (fixed)

The issue #916 write-effect ladder, which `main` added while this branch was open, failed rung R916-01 on the first push of the merged branch: `dishonest report=['reported failure although every declared effect landed']`, baseline 9/9 → 8/9.

Root cause: R916-01 replays the exact issue #905 transport fault (`write_stdin failed: Unknown process id 0`, bytes never land). This branch's recovery path exhausted its bounded per-path retries and then reported the transport message directly, without ever running the check the plan itself had named — so the run ended in a failure report that no observed exit code backed.

Fix: once write recovery is exhausted, run the named verification once; its exit status is what the report carries. Locally the ladder is back to 9/9 (`baseline 9/9 -> now 9/9`), and `an_unrecoverable_write_still_asks_the_workspace_before_reporting` pins the behavior in the unit suite.

body:
Fixes #977.

## The mechanism behind the whole issue

> **A job killed by `timeout-minutes` is reported by GitHub as `cancelled`, not `failure`.**

A run whose only non-success job is `cancelled` inherits the run conclusion `cancelled`, which on the runs list looks exactly like "a human pressed cancel" or "a newer push superseded this run". Grey, not red. No failure notification, no entry in the failed-runs filter.

That is why issue #977 describes the pipeline as `cancelled` rather than `failing`. The pipeline *was* broken — it just never said so.

**18 consecutive `CI/CD Pipeline` runs on `main`** concluded `cancelled` between 2026-08-03T18:09 and 2026-08-06T05:13. The visible damage: the newest GitHub Release was **v0.326.1**, while crates.io already served **0.333.0** and git carried tags for eleven versions in between. **Eleven versions were tagged and published with no GitHub Release at all**, and CI stayed grey through all of it.

## Root causes

### RC1 — `Auto Release` hit its 30-minute cap (run `31065367736`)

| Step | Window |
| --- | --- |
| `cargo build --release` | 02:53:54 → 03:02:08 |
| publish to crates.io (0.333.0) | → 03:04:52 |
| clean-install smoke test | 03:04:53 → 03:13:01 |
| free runner disk | → 03:14:16 |
| `docker buildx build --push` | 03:14:21 → **killed 03:22:04**, still at "Compiling fs2 v0.4.3" |

The PR-check `docker-build` job had used the GHA layer cache all along. The four **release** build-push steps had **no cache at all**, so every release recompiled the whole crate inside Docker — twice with Docker Hub enabled. `Create GitHub Release` sits after the Docker push and was never reached.

### RC2 — `E2E Tests (local web app)` hit its 15-minute cap (run `31073507682`)

`npx playwright install --with-deps chromium` ran **10 min 36 s**. Every library Chromium needs was already *"the newest version"*; the entire time went to apt fetching **font** packages from `azure.archive.ubuntu.com` at ~30–60 KB/s. That left ~4 minutes for `Running 468 tests using 2 workers`; the job died at test 159/468.

**Compounding defect:** `globalTimeout` was `15 * 60_000` — *exactly* the job cap, which also pays for checkout, `bun install`, the bundle build, `npm ci` and the browser install. The job clock always won, so Playwright never aborted, never exited non-zero, `if: failure()` never fired, and **no report artifact was uploaded** — the one artifact that would have explained the run did not exist.

## Changes

**Errors**
- GHA layer cache (`cache-from`/`cache-to: type=gha`) on **all four** release build-push steps.
- `auto-release` / `manual-release`: `timeout-minutes` 30 → 60.
- `--with-deps` split into an `actions/cache`-backed browser install plus a **bounded, non-fatal** `install-deps` step — in **both** `test-e2e-local` and `test-e2e-pages`. Headless Chromium runs without those fonts, so a slow mirror can no longer end the job.
- `test-e2e-local`: `timeout-minutes` 15 → 40; `workers: 4` under CI (one per vCPU; these specs are I/O-bound).

**False negatives**
- `globalTimeout` 15 → 25 min, now well below the 40-minute job cap, so *Playwright* aborts first, exits non-zero, and leaves a report.
- New terminal **`pipeline-status`** job (`scripts/check-pipeline-status.sh`) that `needs:` **every** other job and runs `if: always()`. Any `failure` is fatal; any `cancelled` is fatal **on `main`** — where `cancel-in-progress` is disabled, so a cancellation can only be a timeout or a manual cancel — and a `::warning::` elsewhere, where a supersede is legitimate.

**Warnings**
- Every action off the deprecated Node 20 runtime: `upload-artifact@v4→v7`, `download-artifact@v4→v8`, `setup-node@v4→v6`, `setup-python@v5→v6`, `checkout@v4→v6`, across all workflows.
- `release.yml` was flagged as approaching its 2000-line ceiling. It is now **1948 lines — below its 1960-line starting point** despite gaining a job: six inline `run:` blocks became scripts, two of which (`configure-dockerhub-publishing.sh`, `invoke-create-github-release.sh`) were *byte-identical duplicates* across `auto-release` and `manual-release`.

## Reproducing test

`tests/unit/ci-cd/issue_977.rs` — **all ten assertions fail against the pre-fix tree and pass after** (verified by restoring the original `release.yml` and `playwright.local.config.js` and re-running). It covers: no `--with-deps` in any workflow, browser cache + bounded non-fatal apt step in both e2e jobs, `globalTimeout` < job cap, all four Docker steps cached, release budgets, the gate job's `needs:` covering every job (this caught a job I had missed), the deprecated-action sweep, and the shared-script extraction.

`gate_script_behaves_correctly_for_every_conclusion` runs the gate script for real across success/skipped, cancelled-on-main, cancelled-off-main and failure. `experiments/issue-977-pipeline-status.sh` is the same four cases as a standalone script.

Existing tests in `workflow_release.rs` and `issue_717.rs` were updated to follow the extracted logic into the scripts rather than dropped.

## Evidence and analysis

`dev/log/issues/977/pulls/978/` — both full run logs (25 609 and 31 816 lines) with per-step timings, run/annotation dumps, and **`ANALYSIS.md`** with the timeline, per-requirement root cause, prior art considered (`re-actors/alls-green`, `technote-space/workflow-conclusion-action`) and why a 20-line script fits better.

## Upstream reports

The same defects exist in the pipeline templates, so they are filed there with reproducible examples, workarounds and code fixes:

- link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#118, link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#123, link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#50 — timeout-reported-as-cancelled (all three templates; verified none has an aggregate gate).
- link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#119 — uncached release Docker builds. **Verified as rust-only**: the js and python templates have a single, already-cached build step, so this was not reported against them.

Template job-set diff: the rust template has `cargo-lock`, `coverage`, `deploy-docs` and `fresh-merge` as separate jobs. formal-ai already covers all four — fresh-merge via `scripts/simulate-fresh-merge.sh`, Cargo.lock verification in `lint`, and coverage in its own `coverage.yml` (split out under #895 for the same line-limit reason).

## Local verification

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `shellcheck --severity=warning` over all 18 tracked scripts, `rust-script scripts/check-file-size.rs`, and `cargo test --test unit ci_cd` (**172 passed, 0 failed**) all clean.

## Not addressed, deliberately

- **Recovering the 11 missing GitHub Releases** (v0.326.2 … v0.333.0). The tags and crates.io versions exist; backfilling the Releases is a one-off `gh release create` sweep over historical tags, not a pipeline change, and it rewrites public release history — worth doing, but as its own decision rather than folded into this PR.
- **~25 source files in the 900–1000-line warning band** (`src/main.rs`, `src/solver.rs`, `tests/source/calculation.rs`, …). These are long-standing, predate this issue, and are only warnings; splitting them would be a large, risky refactor unrelated to the CI/CD failures. `scripts/check-file-size.rs` only reports warnings for files that *grew*, so they do not fire on unrelated PRs.

## Summary

Closes #895 (epic #710). CI produced an LCOV file, uploaded it, and never read the numbers — there was no threshold to fail and no way to notice a decrease. This makes the requirement real: coverage is measured, published, and ratcheted.

## What changed

**A non-decreasing ratchet.** `scripts/check-coverage-ratchet.rs` reads the LCOV report, compares each metric against the reviewed floor in `coverage/baseline.json`, and fails the build on a decrease beyond a stated tolerance. Raising a floor is automatic (`--update-baseline`). Lowering one is refused unless `--justification "<reviewed reason>"` is supplied, which is recorded in the baseline as `lowered_reason` — so a decrease reaches review as a sentence in the diff, not two digits changing.

**Published artifacts.** Each denominator emits a human-readable `coverage/summary-<name>.md` (per-metric table, deltas in percentage points, the ten least-covered files) into the run summary, plus a machine-readable `coverage/summary-<name>.json`. Both are uploaded as workflow artifacts with `if: always()`, so a failing run still publishes the numbers that explain the failure.

**Two honest denominators, never averaged.** A Rust percentage and a browser percentage count different things, and one combined number would let a large Rust suite mask an untested website. They are ratcheted separately:

| Denominator | Lines | Functions | Files |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Rust workspace | 86.47% | 44.34% | 408 |
| Browser production JavaScript | 50.48% | 45.54% | 40 |

**Browser coverage, which did not exist before.** `tests/web/` loads the unbundled `src/web/` page scripts and the 24-module worker mirror into a `node:vm` sandbox *under their real repository paths* — which is what makes V8 attribute coverage to the files the browser actually downloads — and boots the worker through its real entry point with the canonical `data/seed/*.lino` corpus behind `fetch`. 48 new tests, run by `npm run test:web` / `npm run coverage:web`.

**The denominator cannot be quietly narrowed.** `coverage/browser-unmeasured.txt` is a committed `path<TAB>reason` inventory of every `src/web/**` file the browser denominator does not measure. A file that is neither measured nor declared fails the build, as does a stale, redundant, or unexplained row. The list can shrink; it cannot grow silently.

**Coverage moved to its own workflow.** `.github/workflows/coverage.yml`, one job per denominator. Nothing in the release graph `needs:` these jobs, so the move changed no ordering; it also returns `release.yml` to 1930 lines, back under the 2000-line ceiling `scripts/check-file-size.rs` documents as debt that must not grow. The triggers, concurrency group, and change-detection gate match release.yml's contract, so a docs-only PR still does not pay for a 25-minute instrumented build.

## Tests

Regression tests for threshold enforcement and baseline updates, as the issue asks:

- **`scripts/check-coverage-ratchet-tests.rs`** — 30 cases run in CI via `rust-script --test scripts/check-coverage-ratchet.rs` in the `lint` job. They pin that a decrease fails, that an improvement only notices, that `--update-baseline` refuses to lower a floor without `--justification`, that an empty denominator is an error rather than a silent 0%, that a missing LCOV file is an error not a pass, that reports are written even when the ratchet breaks, and that the *committed* baseline is valid and carries a real measured floor for both denominators.
- **`tests/unit/ci-cd/workflow_coverage.rs`** — pins the workflow wiring: the gate's own tests run, each denominator is both enforced and published, timeouts and change-gating hold, and (issue #442) no job treats a *skipped* upstream check as a reason to run.

## Verification

Run locally on this branch, all green:

- `cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --lib --bins --tests --all-features && cargo check --examples --all-features && rust-script scripts/check-file-size.rs && rust-script scripts/check-hardcoded-language.rs`
- `rust-script --test scripts/check-coverage-ratchet.rs` — 30 passed
- `npm run coverage:web` then `--only browser` — reproduces the committed browser baseline exactly, ratchet held
- `cargo llvm-cov --all-features --lcov` then `--only rust` — 86.47% / 44.34%, ratchet held

Note on the Rust floor: it was measured from a full local run of the same command `coverage.yml` uses. A handful of integration cases needing outbound network could not complete in the measuring sandbox, so a green CI run measures at or above this floor rather than below it. This is recorded in the baseline's `evidence` field.

## Docs

`docs/design/coverage-ratchet.md` documents the measurement, the publication format, and the baseline-update policy; `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `README.md`, and `REQUIREMENTS.md` point at it.
title: Publish coverage and enforce a non-decreasing coverage ratchet

Closes #894 (child of #710).

The 2026-06-14 four-template CI/CD audit (`docs/case-studies/issue-479/template-comparison/REPORT.md`) ended with *drafted* upstream issues — "Title:", "Body:", "Check:" — and no field in which a filing URL could live. A recommendation with no URL is indistinguishable from an unreported gap and, once the templates move on, from a gap that no longer exists. Two months later four of the report's eight working-repo recommendations had in fact been closed downstream, with no record of it anywhere. Nothing in CI could catch that, because no test read the report.

## What this PR does

**1. Revalidation.** Every finding was re-checked against the current template default branches — `js` `7b70923`, `rust` `c867f78`, `python` `98d6dca`, `csharp` `6806bd9`, all fetched 2026-08-05 — and against the working repo's current `release.yml`. Commands and verbatim output are preserved in `docs/case-studies/issue-894/raw-data/revalidation-greps.txt` and `revalidation-greps-2.txt`.

**2. Filing.** Eight issues filed upstream, each with a reproduction, a workaround and a concrete suggested fix:

| ID | Gap | Issue |
|---|---|---|
| U1-js / U1-rust / U1-python / U1-csharp | No CI security scanning (CodeQL for code *and* GitHub Actions workflows, `dependency-review-action`) | link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#122, link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#115, link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#48, link-foundation/csharp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#43 |
| U2-rust / U2-python / U2-csharp | No broken-link checker; `links.yml` exists only in the JS template | link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#116, link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#49, link-foundation/csharp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#44 |
| U3-rust | No desktop-release workflow / `/download` page — ships the fixed #479 `workflow_run.head_sha` resolver and the electron-builder 26 `mac.identity=-` ad-hoc signing flag as prior art | link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#117 |

All eight bodies are preserved verbatim under `docs/case-studies/issue-894/raw-data/` (`sec-*.md`, `links-*.md`, `desktop-rust.md`), and the created-issue metadata in `filed-upstream-issues.json`.

**3. Ledger.** The report's *Recommended upstream issues to file* section is replaced by *Upstream filing status (revalidated 2026-08-05)*, keyed by finding ID with an explicit status:

- **confirmed** — still reproducible upstream; a filing URL is mandatory (the eight above).
- **not-applicable** — investigated, non-defect: no template references `workflow_run` / `head_sha` (U4), none uses electron-builder or signs macOS bundles (U5), action tag-pinning is a deliberate fleet-wide convention (U6).
- **obsolete** — closed since the snapshot, marked with the evidence that closed it and struck through in the recommendations list: API-docs deploy (L1), published-crate smoke test (L3), resilient buildx (L4), main-safe concurrency (L7).
- **local** — owned by `link-assistant/formal-ai` itself: cargo-lock guard (L2), link checker (L5), multi-OS matrix (L6), security scanning (L8).

**4. Documentation check.** `tests/unit/docs_requirements_issue_894.rs` parses the ledger and fails when a `confirmed` row has no `link-foundation` issue URL, when a status outside the documented vocabulary appears, when the pre-filing recommendation section returns, or when the preserved evidence goes missing.

## Scope note

The acceptance criterion says to file each confirmed gap *in the owning upstream repository*. The four still-open working-repo gaps (L2, L5, L6, L8) are owned by this repository, so they are recorded as `local` in the ledger rather than filed as new `link-assistant/formal-ai` issues. Say the word and I will open them as tracked issues too.

## Verification

```bash
cargo test --test unit docs_requirements_issue_894
# 5 passed
```

The check is falsifiable, and was falsified before being trusted: deleting the U2-rust URL from the ledger fails two of the five tests with

```
row U2-rust is confirmed but has no upstream issue URL; a confirmed finding
may never remain ready-to-file without a filing (issue #894)
```

Also run clean locally: `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --lib --bins --tests --all-features`.

Requirements R894-1 … R894-4 are recorded in `REQUIREMENTS.md`, `docs/requirements-traceability.md` and `docs/case-studies/issue-894/`.

## Summary

- proactively append a seed-backed, localized issue-report consent invitation after unresolved reasoning and detected tool failures
- classify browser/desktop failures from solver intents and structured provider/tool signals, persist the failure bit, and aggregate it across Agent-plan steps
- reuse #839's six-section contextual report action without automatically filing anything
- preserve reproducible red/green browser screenshots, live `@link-assistant/agent` evidence, requirement traceability, and a dedicated Agent CLI CI replay

## Root cause and reproduction

Issue #839 made `Report issue` user-initiated and contextual, but no failure path actively offered it. Unknown reasoning stopped after its diagnostic, structured tool failures only rendered an error, Agent CLI plain-text shell failures could be presented as successful output, and the UI only exposed the old passive action for `intent: unknown`.

```sh
cargo test --test unit issue_864 -- --nocapture
cd tests/e2e && npx playwright test --config=playwright.local.config.js tests/issue-864.spec.js
```

## Summary

- add one seeded software-authoring completion contract shared by Agent, Claude, OpenCode, Codex, Qwen, and Gemini
- require a non-scratch workspace effect before accepting a successful client exit
- escalate through a **seed-declared ladder of recovery strategies** — `restate_postcondition`, `name_target_artifact`, `decompose_into_leaf` — so each retry is a different decomposition rather than a repeat, resuming the native client session when available
- **learn across runs**: every `(client, postcondition, strategy, effect)` triple is appended to a durable ledger outside the caller's workspace, and later runs reorder the ladder to spend what has actually produced artifacts first
- fail closed on public vendor endpoint diversion, now declared in seed data instead of a hardcoded array in `src/`
- emit compact NDJSON with model, endpoint, token, attempt, reason, changed-path, and recovery metadata
- keep `.formal-ai/` scratch state out of completion evidence and Git-visible user changes

## Root cause

`formal-ai with` previously treated the child process exit status as task completion. A client could exit zero after planning, an orientation command, or a no-op response without producing the requested artifact. The wrapper also streamed each client's presentation format directly, so pretty or concatenated JSON was not a stable machine-readable contract.

The earlier revision of this branch closed the gate but retried with a single fixed correction prompt. That is self-healing, not self-learning: a second attempt repeated the same decomposition, and nothing was carried across runs. Issue #879 explicitly asks to "record the (request, plan, outcome) triple and try a different decomposition."

## Generalization

Nothing about the recovery behaviour branches on literals in `src/`:

- the strategy ladder, the attempt budget, the incomplete reason, the scratch directory, and the diverted vendor endpoints are all rows in [`data/seed/client-completion-contracts.lino`](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/issue-879-693050b2608b/data/seed/client-completion-contracts.lino)
- each strategy's correction prompt is a seeded multilingual response (`en`, `ru`, `hi`, `zh`), resolved by the detected request language with an English fallback
- adding a fourth strategy, a seventh client, or a new vendor endpoint is a data edit
- learning may only **reorder** the seeded list — it cannot invent, drop, or exceed it, so a missing or corrupted ledger degrades exactly to the seeded order

## Reproduction and automated coverage

The first commit adds a minimal fake Agent CLI that exits zero, emits pretty JSON with empty metadata, and creates no file. It demonstrates the old false-success behavior before the implementation.

`tests/integration/issue_879_completion.rs` verifies:

- zero exit without an artifact is rejected only after the full bounded ladder, and the three corrections escalate through *distinct* instructions
- `recovery_order_is_learned_from_what_actually_produced_artifacts`: a first run teaches that `name_target_artifact` works and `restate_postcondition` does not; a second run sharing the same state directory spends `name_target_artifact` first, the untried strategy next, and the failed one last — while `strategies_available` is unchanged
- the learning ledger resolves outside the workspace and never appears in `git status`
- a correction can resume the exact native Agent session and complete
- the identical Scala task produces `Hello.scala` through all six registered client adapters, each with its editing profile and local Formal AI endpoint
- English, Russian, Hindi, and Chinese authoring prompts all activate the same workspace-effect contract
- every stdout line is independently parseable JSON with populated endpoint and token metadata
- a reported Codex diversion to `api.openai.com` fails closed
- `.formal-ai/` never satisfies the gate or appears in `git status`

## Live end-to-end evidence

Beyond the deterministic fixtures, the ladder ran against the installed Agent CLI and a temporary local Formal AI server in an empty Git repository, with a request the local model could not satisfy. Session `ses_048503119ffe9cCHeMerd8wBVF` spent all three strategies and the wrapper exited nonzero rather than reporting a false success:


Closes #701.

E59 said the auto-learning loop never closed: it *observed* its failures and stopped. Two symptoms were named, and both were real when measured.

**Symptom 1 — the Trends frontier never moved.** 60 of the 80 committed Google Trends prompts (10 topics × 4 languages × 2 variations) came back `intent: unknown`, run after run, with nothing derived from them.

**Symptom 2 — dreaming amendments were decoration.** `examples/issue_701_amendment_body.rs` reproduces it: solve a prompt plainly, solve it again with a matching retained amendment, strip the appended compliance line, diff the bodies.

```
--- latex: solve a new recurrence proof
plain intent   = unknown
amended intent = unknown
body differs beyond the appended line = false
```

Root cause: `solve_with_amendment_records` prepends a `Standing requirement (...)` user turn, `solve_with_history` records it as a `prior_turn:user` event, and **no downstream handler ever reads it**. The rule reached the log and the prose, never the routing.

## What this PR does

### 1. An adoption contract (R701-1)

`formal-ai learn cycle --frontier google-trends --dry-run [--proposals]` runs one cycle:

```
frontier item → candidate surface → held-out validation → promotion proposal (#656 shape)
```

Candidates are **request-opener surfaces** generalized from ≥2 distinct terms — `… के बारे में बताओ`, `介绍一下 …`, `Дай контекст Google Trends для …` — so a candidate can never be a memorized single prompt. Each is replayed against held-out prompts built from terms it was *not* derived from; one that fails is recorded as blocked, not dropped. One recorded run: 60 frontier items → 6 candidates → 6 validated → 48 held-out tests → 2 proposals. Deterministic and offline.

### 2. Proof of capability delta (R701-2)

`data/meta/learning-adoption-ledger.lino` — **60 before/after pairs, 10 topics, 4 languages**:

```
adoption_pair
  topic "julián andrés quiñones"
  language "en"
  before_intent "unknown"
  before_routed_to "human_triage"
  after_intent "web_search"
  after_query "julián andrés quiñones"
  topic_recovered "true"
  capability_delta "unknown_to_web_search"
```

Tool-authored (`cargo run --release --example issue_701_adoption_ledger`) and byte-pinned against a fresh render.

### 3. The Trends gap, closed (R701-3)

| Measure | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Routed by the engine | 20 | **80** |
| On the learning frontier | 60 | **0** |
| `intent: unknown` rate | 7500 bp | **0 bp** |

Ratcheted by `the_trends_corpus_unknown_rate_is_ratcheted_to_zero`. The 60 pre-adoption verdicts stay frozen in `data/meta/learning-frontier-google-trends.lino` — the gap closing does not erase the evidence it existed.

### 4. The decoration-only path, deleted (R701-4)

A retained standing requirement now changes how a task is **classified**, which a string append cannot do: a covered task the solver could not otherwise route is no longer returned as unresolved, and it cites the amendment as evidence. The three application paths (solver, memory recall, agentic final) were collapsed onto one selection rule (`matching_amendments`) and one projection (`amendment_lines`); the duplicated `matching_amendment_lines` decorator is gone.

`tests/unit/issue_701_dreaming_amendment_class.rs` raises the single-prompt #540 check into a class:

- 3 topics × 4 languages of **held-out paraphrases** through both `create_chat_completion_with_solver_and_memory` and `create_response_with_solver_and_memory`;
- a covered task is never reported unresolved;
- a **negative control** — an uncovered task must come back byte-identical to the empty-memory answer, so "the answer changed" is evidence of something.

### 5. Periodic, proposal-only, human-gated (R701-5)

- In-process: every idle dreaming run writes a learning-cycle record next to the memory log.
- Scheduled CI: `.github/workflows/learning-cycle.yml` runs daily, publishes proposals as an artifact, and asserts `mode "proposal_only"`, `human_gated "true"`, and `git diff --exit-code -- data/seed`. A cycle that stops proposing anything fails the job rather than passing quietly.

### 6. Durable failure records (R701-6)

Frozen frontier record plus blocked classes in the cycle record; nothing is silently dropped (R425).

## Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Result |
| --- | --- |
| ≥1 valid promotion proposal with tests, deterministic and offline | 2 proposals, 6 validated candidates, 48 held-out tests |
| Ledger ≥20 pairs / ≥3 topics / 4 languages | 60 pairs, 10 topics, 4 languages |
| Regression test on a **held-out paraphrase** | `retained_amendments_change_held_out_answers_across_topics_and_languages` (12 paraphrases, both surfaces) |
| `intent: unknown` rate drops and is ratcheted | 7500 bp → 0 bp, ratcheted |

## Honest narrowings

- The cycle derives one *class* of knowledge — request-opener surfaces — because that is the class the recorded frontier actually consists of. The contract is class-agnostic; the tested coverage is not, and we do not claim otherwise.
- Requirement 4's delta is a change in routing and evidence, not a rewrite of the answer body by the standing rule. A deterministic engine cannot invent a body from a rule it has no handler for; claiming it did would be the decoration problem in a new costume.

## Merge integration and verification

Merged `main` at release `v0.312.0`. The integration exposed and fixed two concrete mainline interactions:

- the added learning subcommand pushed `src/main.rs` over its hard 1,000-line gate, so learning argument parsing and dispatch now live together in `src/cli_learn.rs` and the self-AST census was regenerated;
- the `v0.312.0` release consumed issue #844's changelog fragment, while its traceability test still required the deleted pre-release file. The test now follows the repository's established fragment-or-released-`CHANGELOG.md` lifecycle.

The first exact-merge CI run also exposed two independent stability bugs, both reproduced before fixing:

- macOS ARM64 packaging completed signing and ZIP creation, then the runner's disk-image service returned `hdiutil: attach failed - Device not configured`. The existing bounded retry recognized the documented transient only during `create`; it now recognizes the same signatures during `attach`, with a regression test that still proves arbitrary packaging failures fail fast.
- release asset resolution could count all 17 required assets and still report one missing: under `set -o pipefail`, `printf ... | grep -q` can convert an early successful match into failure when `printf` receives SIGPIPE. The membership probe now feeds `grep` directly, backed by a deterministic 3,017-name regression test.

- `cargo test --doc --verbose`, strict Clippy with `-D warnings`, formatting, and all-feature example checks passed.
- All repository policy scripts passed, including file size, changelog, hardcoded-language, worker-line, disk-usage, terminology, and WASM-size gates.

- Case study: `docs/case-studies/issue-701/README.md`, `requirements.md`
- Online research (Reflexion, Voyager, curriculum learning — with the non-transfer list): `docs/case-studies/issue-701/raw-data/online-research.md`

Closes #842.

## Summary

- Turns the issue #840 dataset into a strict, appendable 24-node quality ratchet for reports #838, #827, and #826.
- Fixes the two false greens exposed by stronger judging: multilingual definition-example requests now share one slot-driven route, and an isolated contextual pronoun asks for its missing antecedent instead of searching the web.
- Filters flattened web evidence by language-independent sentence structure so navigation fragments and adjacent headings are not repeated as an answer.
- Separates assistant-authored claims from raw tool evidence and judges positive assertions, alternatives, refusals, capability menus, tool routes, and shell-command shape.
- Derives evidence-bearing failure-learning proposals on every run while keeping promotion explicitly human-gated.
- Runs the full stable-ID ratchet in its own bounded, least-privilege CI workflow and retains both measurements and learning proposals.
- Pins sccache 0.16.0 after the newly released 0.17.0 expanded Rust response files past the Windows command-line limit; workflow regression coverage prevents another silent tool-version upgrade.

## Measured outcome

The historical v0.303.0 baseline passed **8/24**. The final strict measurement passes **24/24**:

| Slice | Historical | Final |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Total | 8/24 | **24/24** |
| L1 — original requests | 1/3 | **3/3** |
| L2 | 1/6 | **6/6** |
| L3 | 2/7 | **7/7** |
| L4 — atomic subtasks | 4/8 | **8/8** |
| #838 local discovery | 3/10 | **10/10** |
| #827 definition/follow-up | 1/7 | **7/7** |
| #826 comparison/report | 4/7 | **7/7** |

L1 and L4 now both pass at 100%, removing the reported composition/decomposition inversion.

## Root cause and generalized production rules

The earlier harness allowed raw tool output to satisfy answer assertions and did not require positive answer evidence or route parity on every node. Re-judging the existing responses exposed two real failures:

- `827.L4.a` returned the generic Russian unknown fallback because “give an example of X” had no agentic research route.
- `827.L4.b` searched the public web for the pronoun `это` even though the request supplied no antecedent.

Regression tests were added first. The production fix is structural:

- `definition_example_request` is one slotted meaning role. English and Russian use prefix slots, Hindi uses a suffix slot, and Chinese uses a circumfix slot. The planner extracts the subject from slot structure, so another language or phrasing is a seed-data extension rather than a prompt-specific Rust branch.
- A parsed concept query whose subject is a non-referential pronoun and whose only context is a sentence returns the existing localized clarification.
- Fetched evidence prefers complete prose blocks identified by script-level sentence terminals. If no complete block exists, the ordinary relevance path retains all evidence, preserving terse legitimate answers without a provider-specific phrase blocklist.

Focused Rust coverage is in `tests/unit/issue_842.rs`.

## A falsifiable, growing ladder

`experiments/issue_840_task_ladder/ladder.py` now records and judges:

- assistant output independently from the complete tool transcript;
- `expect`, `expect_any`, and `forbid` answer assertions;
- required and forbidden tool routes;
- forbidden command fragments;
- execution errors, exact generic refusals, and capability-menu fallbacks.

The offline web fixture deliberately includes page controls and adjacent headings. Those strings are forbidden in answers, so successful routing alone cannot masquerade as synthesis.

The baseline comparison is per stable task ID. It rejects a removed node, a previously green node that regresses, or any failing appended node. New maintainer reports extend the graph with new IDs and can advance `results.json` only after all old and new nodes pass.

Every failed observation also becomes a proposal containing its stable ID, prompt, assistant output, tools, commands, error, and exact violated assertions. Proposals remain `awaiting_human_review`; the harness cannot promote behavior or move the baseline itself.

## Real clients and Formal AI self-application

The final release binary passed the representative OpenCode TUI node and the complete real Agent CLI journeys for local discovery, definition/follow-up research, comparison, and Russian report creation.

The reviewed issue decomposition names five smallest leaves. Formal AI, through the real Agent CLI, authored and verified the durable stable-ID invariant leaf (**1/5 = 20%**); the other four remain honestly attributed to human tool extension. Session `ses_052c4f066ffecNc3GC3Dk13wJ9` and its raw stream, server trace, decomposition, and byte-identical artifact are retained under `docs/case-studies/issue-842/self-hosting/`.

The complete rationale and reproducible evidence map are in `docs/case-studies/issue-842/README.md`.

This PR adds an end-to-end harness for real, unmodified upstream benchmark
slices. It downloads revision-pinned payloads at run time, grades each suite by
its actual semantic criterion, publishes the measured `passed / total` without
floors or score substitution, and prevents regressions with a base-aware
per-suite ratchet.

## Honest retained measurement

Slice 20, solver `0.300.0`, recorded 2026-07-20:

| Suite | License | Retained result | Criterion |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| HumanEval | MIT | **0 / 20** | upstream `check(entry_point)` |
| MBPP | Apache-2.0 | **0 / 20** | upstream `test_list` assertions |
| GSM8K | MIT | **2 / 20** | final number after `####` |
| MATH (`prm800k` split) | MIT | **0 / 20** | final boxed answer |
| BIG-bench `object_counting` | Apache-2.0 | **0 / 20** | upstream target number |
| CoEdIT | Apache-2.0 | **0 / 20** | normalized upstream target text |
| EditEval | — | `benchmark_unavailable` | no distributable permissive task payload |
| SWE-bench Lite | MIT | `benchmark_unavailable` | historical gold-diff proxy withdrawn |

The raw historical log still contains a SWE-bench `0 / 20` investigation line,
but the committed ledger deliberately does not treat it as a score. Gold-patch
equality is not SWE-bench. A valid future result is recorded only when the
pinned official evaluator applies the candidate patch and executes repository
tests in its upstream container.

## Implementation

- Immutable suite registry and runtime cache: Git/Hugging Face revisions,
  payload URL, byte length, and FNV-64 content id are persisted in provenance
  sidecars and revalidated before reuse. No upstream dataset is vendored.
- Suite-native grading: Python tests for HumanEval/MBPP, numeric and boxed
  comparisons for reasoning suites, exact normalized text for CoEdIT, and the
  official SWE-bench evaluator pinned at

- Explicit unavailability: download, parse, short-payload, missing evaluator,
  and evaluator-infrastructure failures become `benchmark_unavailable`; no
  repository-authored proxy or gold-patch shortcut receives a score.
- Honest ledger and ratchet: `minimum_pass_count` equals the best measured
  result. Pull requests compare the ledger with `origin/${GITHUB_BASE_REF}`;
  the scheduled job runs bounded core slices plus a separately bounded
  container-heavy SWE-bench slice.

  converted through Formal AI's shared associative-memory substrate into
  ranked proposal artifacts. They remain `awaiting_human_review`; measurements

## Reproduction

Before this change, a freely phrased procedure such as:

> When I paste a link, fetch its title, translate it to Russian, save both, and reply with the translation.

## Root cause and upstream release

The original Formal AI prototype used a process wrapper plus a local xterm renderer. It could not provide a portable child PTY, propagate terminal resize correctly, preserve scrollback as ordered states, or create a faithful publishable replay without owning a private terminal stack.

The reusable implementation was moved upstream and released before Formal AI consumed it:

| Responsibility | Published release | Merged work |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Generic PTY execution, typed input/resize, VT rendering, scrollback, unrolling, asciicast, exact-grid SVG/GIF replay, timeout artifacts, and visible-text geometry | [`command-stream` 0.17.2](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/releases/tag/js-v0.17.2) | [#176](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/pull/176), [#177](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/pull/177), [#179](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/pull/179), [#181](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/pull/181), [#184](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/pull/184), [#186](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/pull/186) |
| Agent-specific executable/argument builders, startup interactions, semantic events, and 4:3 replay bundles | [`agent-commander` 0.10.1](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent-commander/releases/tag/js_0.10.1) | [#44](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent-commander/pull/44), [#45](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent-commander/pull/45), [#47](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent-commander/pull/47), [#49](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent-commander/pull/49) |

The final Chromium review exposed one more upstream defect: blank cells at the edges of a row were emitted inside visible SVG `<text>` runs, so the browser stretched short labels across the terminal width. A minimum published-package regression reproduced that bug in [`command-stream#185`](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/issues/185). [`command-stream#186`](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/pull/186) removes only edge padding while retaining internal blanks and exact cell geometry; it was merged, released as 0.17.2, and then consumed here.

Fresh CI then exposed a clean-consumer packaging defect in `agent-commander` 0.10.0: its published manifest retained a development-only `postinstall` hook and an obsolete patch, so hoisted npm consumers could not install it. The failure was reduced to a clean tarball-consumer test in [`agent-commander#48`](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent-commander/issues/48). [`agent-commander#49`](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent-commander/pull/49) removed the published hook/patch, added Node, Bun, and Deno consumer coverage, and was released as 0.10.1 before this branch consumed it.

## Reproduction and automated regression

The focused regression uses a two-row terminal so the first state must scroll out of the viewport. It requires the unrolled transcript to contain the user, tool, and result states once each and in order. A second fixture accepts text (`123`), Tab, Enter, and a `24×6 → 40×10` resize, and succeeds only after the child PTY observes the new dimensions.

The published replay regression additionally requires:

- no leading or trailing terminal padding inside any visible SVG text run;
- embedded terminal font data and integer cell-grid geometry;
- timestamp-derived CSS keyframes rather than lossy SVG animation elements;
- square terminal framing and preserved whitespace;
- a valid GIF89a fallback;
- partial replay artifacts after timeout.

Run it with:

```bash
cd experiments/agent_cli_e2e/issue_819_tui
bun install --frozen-lockfile
bun test
```

The complete live matrix passed locally:

```text
Agent direct
OpenCode direct
Claude Code direct
Codex direct
OpenCode TUI + replay × 2
Claude Code TUI + replay × 2
Codex TUI + replay × 2
```

Every TUI run proves `user prompt → assistant find call → client tool result → assistant final path`, starts at 80×30, resizes after the result, and produces all six artifact types. The six normalized observations become three independently worded client groups and 42 stable proposals:

```text
6 observations
  → 3 independent client/capability groups
    → stable intersection per field
      → 42 proposals
        → awaiting_human_review
```

No proposal is applied automatically. A separate E2E asks Formal AI, through a real Agent CLI, to execute exactly `formal-ai clients learn`; the Agent-authored result must match the deterministic report byte for byte.

The same OpenCode result rendered in Chromium before the upstream stack, with the padded-text defect, and after 0.17.2:

| Lossy local prototype | Published 0.17.1 padded rows | Published 0.17.2 |

## Summary

- Audits Formal AI's current legal/compliance posture and records the truthful
  starting state: this repository ships symbolic software, not trained neural
  weights, and has no approved training or distillation sources.
- Adds a conservative, fail-closed
  [legal/compliance policy](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/issue-834-14f41fd75c97/LEGAL-COMPLIANCE.md)
  covering public-domain contributions, third-party rights, closed APIs,
  personal data, prohibited uses, the EU AI Act, regional review triggers, and
  warranty limits.
- Adds a canonical
  [training-source registry](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/issue-834-14f41fd75c97/data/training/source-registry.json),
  source-review form, and executable equality gate. Every future
  parameter-updating artifact must have an approved, non-empty 43-field record;
  undocumented artifacts fail CI.
- Tightens the contribution guide and PR template against leaked/proprietary
  code, unauthorized paid/access-controlled data, large copyrighted payloads,
  secrets, and real personal data.
- Answers the issue's Llama 3.3, Mistral 7B, OpenRouter, and regional-law
  questions using exact-version, provider-route, and primary-source analysis.

## Audit result

The repository had useful isolated controls—the Unlicense, benchmark
provenance, runtime-source records, and personal-event-log boundaries—but no
inbound public-domain submission rule and no enforceable training-source
intake. This change closes that engineering gap without claiming worldwide
legal clearance.

Benchmark fixtures, runtime retrieval/cache data, and community examples are
now explicitly separate from training data. Changing their purpose requires a
new review. The empty registry is paired with
`current_state: "no-approved-training-sources"` and an exact recursive
artifact/registry comparison, so it cannot be treated as implicit approval.

The full findings, before/after matrix, primary research, and residual counsel
boundary are preserved in the
[issue #834 case study](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/issue-834-14f41fd75c97/docs/case-studies/issue-834/README.md).

The issue asks for every false positive, false negative, warning and error in CI/CD. ## The two failures that were actually red

**1. `Auto Release` deadlocked on the self-hosting ratchet.** Two independent root causes:

- *The denominator measured log volume, not authorship.* 599,340 of the 636,240 lines in `v0.300.0..main` — **94.20%** — were captured CI transcripts and lockfiles that this repository *requires* each iteration to commit. Committing the evidence the process demands was itself scored as a regression, so the ratchet could only ever tighten past reach. Artifacts (`*.log`, `*.jsonl`, `*.diff`, `*.patch`, `*.stderr`, `*.stdout`) and lockfiles are now excluded symmetrically from both sides of the ratio, under a new `METRIC_VERSION = 2` so the change starts a fresh comparison epoch instead of silently invalidating recorded history.
- *Enforcement sat where nobody could act on it.* It ran in `record_release`, on `main`, after every contributing commit was already immutable — and it blocked the only mechanism that advances the range. Release-time is now `RatchetPolicy::Report`; enforcement moved to a differential (branch-vs-base) pull-request gate, where the commits can still be amended.

Verified: the exact command that failed in CI now exits 0 — `4.36% (1608/36896 changed lines; 10/119 commits)`.

**2. macOS desktop codesigning.** Not a packaging defect. Run 29752745259 is a `workflow_run` *healing* build of tag `v0.300.0`, which predates the four packaging fixes already merged; the fixed code is proven green in PR run 29746221627 (`considered=1479 skipped=751`). It needs a newer tag, which fix 1 unblocks. Rather than leave this to be re-diagnosed every time, `scripts/desktop-release-resolve.sh` now emits a `::notice` when it is packaging a tag that is not the tip of the default branch.

## Checks that never gated

| What | Why it was green |
| --- | --- |
| `cargo clippy` | Ran without `-D warnings`. Every lint in `[lints.clippy]` is `warn`, so the job printed findings and exited 0. The tree is clean today, so adding it promotes existing behaviour rather than introducing failures. |
| `scripts/check-file-size.rs` | Matched directory exclusions as **substrings**, so `.git` hid all of `.github/workflows/**`. Exclusions are now matched per path component; workflows are measured (warn 1500, fail 2000), while third-party workflows quoted under `docs/case-studies/**` stay exempt — reformatting them would destroy the thing they document. |
| workflow definitions and shell scripts | Nothing validated either. A mistyped `needs.<job>` reference fails **open**: the guarded step silently skips under a green check. `actionlint` 1.7.7 (shellcheck-embedded) and `shellcheck --severity=warning` now run in `lint`. |
| desktop library tests | `node --test $(ls … \| grep -v …)` fell back to Node's own discovery whenever the glob stopped matching — a green step running none of the intended tests. The list is built explicitly and an empty list is a hard error. |

## Checks that gated the wrong thing

- `auto-release`/`manual-release` needed only `[lint, test, build]`. A red **`Secrets Scan`** or either E2E suite on `main` still published the crate, the Docker image and the GitHub Release. (`docker-build` is deliberately *not* a gate: it publishes independently and its failure must not block the crate.)
- The desktop `finalize` job ran under `always()`, so a **cancelled** run could `gh release upload --clobber` a partial `SHA256SUMS.txt` over a complete one. Now `!cancelled()`.
- Desktop packaging and VS Code jobs validated a stale merge preview; they now simulate the fresh merge, as `lint`/`test` already did.
- `secretlint` floated to whatever `latest` was at run time. Pinned.
- `$BASE_REF` was unquoted in `scripts/simulate-fresh-merge.sh` — a word-split there takes the *skip* branch and reports success without merging.
- `upload-pages-artifact` dropped dotfiles (`include-hidden-files: true`); the screenshot upload was `if: always()` with the default `if-no-files-found: warn`, i.e. green on an empty artifact.

One finding was deliberately **not** "fixed": `scripts/install.sh` is the only script without `pipefail`, because it is the only one running under `#!/usr/bin/env sh`. `pipefail` is not POSIX and aborts dash — the `/bin/sh` a `curl … | sh` install lands in. The rationale is now recorded in the file header so it is not "fixed" later.

## Upstream reports

Three defects reproduce in the templates themselves; all were re-verified against upstream `main` via the API before reporting.

- link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#111 — **filed in this iteration**: unquoted `$BASE_REF` in `simulate-fresh-merge.sh`, with a reproduction, a workaround and a suggested fix. (The rust template's copy quotes correctly; python does not ship the script.)
- link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#33 and #35 — already open upstream, so recorded rather than re-filed.

## Verification

- `cargo test --test unit` → **1953 passed, 0 failed** (6 new regression tests)
- `actionlint -shellcheck` over every workflow → exit 0 (type-checking confirmed live by injecting a bogus `needs.secrets-scanX` into a copy and observing the error)
- `shellcheck --severity=warning` over the 17 shipped scripts → exit 0
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `rust-script scripts/check-file-size.rs` → exit 0

New tests: `releases_do_not_publish_past_a_failing_secrets_scan_or_e2e_suite`, `lint_job_gates_on_workflow_shell_and_clippy_findings`, `check_directory_measures_github_workflows`, `check_directory_does_not_measure_quoted_case_study_workflows`, plus the ratchet exclusion and differential-gate tests.

## Debug output (default off, per the issue)

- `FORMAL_AI_MACOS_SIGN_DEBUG=1` — per-path `[adhoc-sign-mac]` sign decisions; its *absence* from the failing log is what proved the healing-build diagnosis.
- `experiments/self_hosting_ratchet_replay/replay.py` — per-commit attribution, reason and subject for any range, without `rust-script`.

## Second pass: defects found by running the fixed pipeline

Run [29767811026](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/runs/29767811026) was the first full run of the repaired pipeline, and it found two more — one introduced by this PR's own first commit.

**`Test (ubuntu-latest)` reported failure with 1953 tests passed and 0 failed.** The suite finished at 18:43:50; `timeout-minutes: 15` killed the job 1.1 seconds later, during teardown. Run 29749095334 on `main` had already done exactly this and was never diagnosed, because GitHub renders a timeout as `cancelled` — indistinguishable from an infrastructure blip. The budget was not padding: checkout plus the two data checks cost ~3m15s before a test runs, the suite takes ~11m, and eight individual agentic/driver tests each exceed 60 s. Recent `main` durations show creep rather than a one-off — 11m02s, 12m27s, 11m49s, 12m57s, **15m16s (cancelled)**, 14m13s. The budget now matches measured cost, and the step emits a `::warning` past 70% of it so the margin cannot be eaten again in silence. Making those eight tests cheaper is separate work with its own regression risk; what is fixed here is the false report.

**The release gates I added would have accepted a timed-out job.** They read `needs.<job>.result != 'failure'`, chosen so a legitimately *skipped* job would not block a release — but the finding above is the proof that a timeout resolves to `'cancelled'`, which is also `!= 'failure'`. Both gates now enumerate the two acceptable results, and the regression test asserts the positive form *and* that the weaker spelling is absent.

**Both fixes were then swept across every job, not just where they had fired.** No `needs.<job>.result != 'failure'` comparison remains in either workflow. Every declared cap was measured against its worst observed run: `coverage` was at **94%** of its 15-minute budget (11m02s → 14m06s across the last eight `main` runs) — one run from the identical false failure — and `lint` at 78% after the new checks accumulated; both were raised, each carrying its measurements inline so the number is auditable rather than arbitrary. `test-e2e-local` (63%) and `docker-build` (23%) have real headroom and were left alone.

That run also independently confirmed the rest: `Self-Hosting Evidence Check` green **on the real PR**, every new lint step green, and [Desktop Release 29767811373](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/runs/29767811373) green across all six platform legs including both macOS architectures — the confirmation that current desktop code signs and packages fine, and that run 29752745259 failed only because it was a healing build of the older `v0.300.0` tag.
