Fixes #810

Full evidence and analysis: [`dev/log/issues/810/pulls/811/analysis.md`](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/issue-810-9b3071713a8e/dev/log/issues/810/pulls/811/analysis.md)

## What was failing

Both default-branch runs named in the issue are at `bd0bac88`. Every job passed except:

| Run | Job |
| --- | --- |
| [29737218421](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/runs/29737218421) CI/CD Pipeline | Auto Release |
| [29738571290](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/runs/29738571290) Desktop Release | Build macos-arm64 / macos-x64 (+ SHA256SUMS cascade) |

Two independent defects.

## Defect A — the evidence gate deadlocked every release (fixed)

```
Error recording self-hosting release metric: no committed Formal-AI-Evidence
in 10e65ae2 records session issue-804-claude-20260720
```

`scripts/self-hosting-metric.rs` requires an evidence document to contain its own session id. Commit `10e65ae2`'s does not (`git show 10e65ae2:…/analysis.md | grep -c issue-804-claude-20260720` → `0`).

The timeline is what makes this fatal: the `evidence-check` gate was added in `39fdef91`, **after** `10e65ae2` merged. `record_release` measures `<last tag>..HEAD`, so that commit sits in the release range until a new tag is cut — and cutting a tag requires the release to succeed. Closed loop; no future commit could fix it.

**Fix:** an explicit `EvidencePolicy`. The pull-request gate stays `Strict` and still hard-fails new malformed records before they reach `main`. `record_release` is `Lenient`: it warns and leaves the commit unattributed, so the metric can only ever under-report, never over-report.

**Test:** `a_malformed_historical_evidence_record_cannot_deadlock_a_release` reproduces the exact shape of `10e65ae2` and asserts both halves — `measure()` still errors, `record_release()` succeeds with `self_authored_commits == 0`. `5 passed; 0 failed`.

## Defect B — bundled Chrome framework seal (instrumented, not yet fixed)

```
…/Contents/Resources/browser-runtime/Frameworks/Google Chrome for Testing Framework.framework:
  unsealed contents present in the root directory of an embedded framework
```

The logs prove the custom sign hook **was** invoked (electron-builder's own `• executing custom sign` marker, plus `--timestamp=none` from our `optionsForFile`), but contain **zero** `[adhoc-sign-mac]` lines despite `FORMAL_AI_MACOS_SIGN_DEBUG=1`. So it is still unknown whether the ignore predicate was consulted and said "sign it" or was never called — the two need different fixes, and guessing between them is how the previous two attempts went.

Per the issue's instruction to add diagnostics when the data is insufficient:

- `log()` now writes via `fs.writeSync(2, …)`. Async `process.stderr.write()` on a pipe loses whatever is queued when electron-builder aborts; a synchronous fd-2 write cannot. If the banner is still missing next run, the executing module is not this one.
- The ignore predicate carries `stats`, reported as `ignore predicate: considered=N skipped=M` from a `finally` block, so it is emitted **on failure too**. `considered=0` vs `skipped=0` are very different diagnoses.
- The per-file trace stays behind `FORMAL_AI_MACOS_SIGN_DEBUG`, **off by default**. Only two summary lines are unconditional.

The analysis document also argues that the durable fix is structural — ship the browser runtime as an archive expanded on first launch, so `codesign` never walks into a bundle it did not lay out — rather than further ignore-rule tuning.

## Deliberately not done

- **Upstream reports.** The `@electron/osx-sign` array-`ignore` behaviour is real and already worked around in-repo, but filing before the counters land would be filing a guess.
- **Template comparison** against the three `link-foundation/*-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template` repos. Neither observed failure originates in template-derived workflow structure, so this is separate work; it is recorded as an open gap in §5 of the analysis rather than silently dropped.

---

## Second iteration — two flakes on this branch (both fixed)

Run [29742025207](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/runs/29742025207) failed `Code Coverage` and `E2E Tests (agent CLI ↔ formal-ai)`. Neither is caused by this branch's diff, and both pass on `main` — they are nondeterministic false negatives, which requirement 3 of the issue covers explicitly. Analysis §6.

**Defect C — `desktop_release_resolve` unit test (`1937 passed; 1 failed`).** The test writes a mock `gh` into a scratch `PATH` dir and immediately executes it. The unit suite is multi-threaded, so a `Command` spawn in another thread can fork between the mock's `write` and its `close` and inherit the write descriptor; `execve` on an inode held open for writing fails with `ETXTBSY`. `desktop-release-resolve.sh` swallowed a failed `gh` (`|| true`), so the asset query degraded silently to "no assets exist" and `should_build` flipped `false` → `true` — the exact observed values. Fixes: the mock is published via `rename`, the script now distinguishes a failed query from an empty one (decision unchanged; both build, the fail-safe direction), and the assertion prints the script's stdout.

**Defect D — agent CLI E2E (`!! report request did not execute gh`).** The research turn fetched three live pages and grew the transcript to a 246 KB request; opencode then summarised the session mid-run, and the next turn reached the server with `"Continue if you have next steps"` instead of `"Report this problem"` (`agentic_outcome: fallthrough (task unrecognised)`). Whether this triggers depends on what fec.gov / usatoday / wikipedia serve that day. The advertised context limit is a harness knob the server never enforces, so it is raised out of reach; a diagnostic branch now names compaction explicitly if it recurs.

## Template comparison (requirement 7 — was the open gap)

Cloned all three `link-foundation/*-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template` repos, diffed their workflows against ours, and re-checked both workflows against `CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md`. Analysis §7 records everything. One real false negative found and fixed: `desktop-release.yml`'s PR `paths` filter omitted `src/**`, `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock`, even though the build job compiles and bundles the `formal-ai` binary — so a Rust-only change could break desktop packaging with a green PR. Two flagged items were checked and rejected as non-issues (with the verifying command recorded), and two genuine-but-larger gaps are written down rather than silently dropped.

## Summary

Fixes the CI/CD defects behind issue #808 and moves the checks that previously
only ran on `main` into the pull-request stage, so a pull request can no longer
be green while the release it produces is broken.

Fixes #808

## Root causes found (evidence in `dev/log/issues/808/pulls/809/`)

1. **macOS codesign failure on release** — `codesign` refused the bundled Chrome
   for Testing runtime ("unsealed contents present in the root directory of an
   embedded framework"): its framework layout is not versioned. Fixed with
   `mac.signIgnore`, independently of the custom sign hook.
2. **The macOS sign hook produced no output at all** — this was unexplained, so
   the first commit added an unconditional hook-entry banner and routed the
   diagnostics to stderr. On the first pull-request packaging run that
   instrumentation answered it: `app-builder-lib`'s `isSignAllowed()` returns
   early with *"Current build is a part of pull request, code signing will be
   skipped"* whenever `GITHUB_BASE_REF` is set, so the hook is never invoked and
   the app ships without a `CodeResources` envelope. Fixed with
   `CSC_FOR_PULL_REQUEST` on the ad-hoc step only (no secrets are in play there).
3. **Auto Release blocked by a malformed self-hosting evidence trailer** — now
   validated at pull-request time by a new `evidence-check` job.

## All checks now run at the pull-request stage (issue comment 5020083365)

- Desktop + `.vsix` packaging: the full six-target matrix, macOS signing and the
  artifact smoke tests run on pull requests in **dry-run** mode — every
  publishing step (attest, release upload, `SHA256SUMS`, `finalize`) is skipped.
  Path-filtered so unrelated pull requests do not pay for six runners.
- Docker image build + `verify-formal-ai-dind` runtime contract (`push: false`,
  so it is fork-safe).
- Self-hosting evidence trailers.
- Secrets scan.
- Fresh-merge simulation against the current `main`.

## Practices adopted from the pipeline templates (R3/R5)

Compared against `link-foundation/{rust,js,python}-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template`
and `hive-mind/docs/CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md`:

- `scripts/simulate-fresh-merge.sh` (verbatim from the js template) — a stale
  merge preview now fails the pull request instead of breaking `main`.
- `scripts/check-secrets.sh` + `.secretlintrc.json`. Scoped to the files a change
  touches: the template's `secretlint "**/*"` did not finish in 25 minutes on
  this tree, while the diff scan measures 2.6 s. Verified it actually fires — a
  planted `ghp_…` token is reported as `[GITHUB_TOKEN] found GitHub Token`.
- `.github/actions/setup-buildx-resilient` (verbatim from the rust template),
  replacing all three raw `docker/setup-buildx-action@v4` uses.
- Replaced all nine `always() && !cancelled()` guards with `!cancelled()`
  (best-practices §10): `always()` also runs the job when the run is *cancelled*,
  which is the opposite of the intent.

## Defects reported upstream (R4)

Four issues filed with reproducible examples, workarounds and code suggestions —
see §8 of the analysis for the table and for two self-corrections I made while
verifying my own earlier claims.

## Verification

- `cargo test --test unit ci_cd::` — 131 passed. The workflow-invariant tests
  were updated for the new jobs rather than around them.
- `bash scripts/check-secrets.sh`, `bash scripts/simulate-fresh-merge.sh` and
  `rust-script scripts/self-hosting-metric.rs --since main --until HEAD` all run
  clean locally.
- Regression test asserting the `mac.signIgnore` patterns match the browser
  runtime and not the app binary.

## Summary

Fixes #664 — the product's associative surface is a **links network**, not a "graph". This PR completes the terminology cleanup across the public API, source tree, UI, and docs, adds a hygiene lint that blocks *new* graph-named public surfaces, and keeps the legacy `/v1/graph` route alive as a deprecated alias so existing clients keep working.

## What changed (per acceptance requirement)

**1. Canonical `/v1/network` endpoint + deprecated `/v1/graph` alias**
- `GET /v1/network` (and `/api/formal-ai/v1/network`) is now the canonical links-network projection: same nodes/edges, `?trace=` filtering, `?format=dot` export, 404-on-unknown-trace.
- `GET /v1/graph` keeps working but is flagged deprecated: identical payload, plus a wire `deprecation: true` header and a `link: </v1/network>; rel="successor-version"` header.
- Integration test `tests/integration/issue_664_network_alias.rs` exercises the real loopback HTTP server and asserts byte-identical payloads, the deprecation marker on the alias, and its absence on the canonical route.

**2. Source renames**
- `src/self_source_graph.rs` → `src/self_source_links.rs`
- `src/agentic_coding/source_graph.rs` → `src/agentic_coding/source_links.rs`
- All module references, doc comments, examples, and tests updated accordingly.

**3. UI string sweep → "links network view"**
- Web, desktop, and VS Code surfaces now say "links network view"; the seeded user-facing "graph" concept (issue #161) is preserved as a synonym, not deleted.

**4. Repository-hygiene lint** — `scripts/check-associative-terminology.rs`
- Blocks *new* graph-named public API routes and Rust `mod` declarations / source-file names, wired into the release workflow's Lint job and registered in the ci-cd unit suite.
- Scoped narrowly to versioned API route prefixes (`/v1/`, `/api/formal-ai/v1/`) and Rust module/file names, so legitimate internal graph-theory identifiers (`substitution_graph`, `GraphNode`, `graphql`, `ideographic`) and prose are never flagged.

- **Acceptance:** fails on a fixture introducing `/v1/knowledge-graph` (covered by `new_knowledge_graph_route_is_flagged` and `check_directory_flags_fixture_and_respects_scope`).

**5. Docs + changelog**
- `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `README.md`, and `REQUIREMENTS.md` updated to links-network terminology (`/v1/network` canonical, `/v1/graph` deprecated). Fixed the stale `src/graph.rs` reference in `REQUIREMENTS.md` R81 (the endpoint lives in `handle_network_request` in `src/network_endpoint.rs`).
- Internal graph-theory prose (formalized graph, `doublets-rs` graph, `SubstitutionGraph`) is intentionally preserved.
- Added changelog fragment `changelog.d/20260714_120000_issue_664_links_network_terminology.md` (`bump: minor`).

- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` ✅ (no new warnings)
- `cargo test` ✅ (1576 passed, 0 failed, doc-tests ok)
- `rust-script scripts/check-associative-terminology.rs` ✅

Fixes #796.

Two independent root causes — both **false positives** — landed on merge commit `12a4b34e` and together produced what looked like one broad CI collapse.

Full investigation, logs and evidence: [`dev/log/issues/796/pulls/797/`](dev/log/issues/796/pulls/797/).

## Root cause A — version-pinned npm deprecation allowlist

Every job that installs Node dependencies failed with exit code 1 *after* npm itself succeeded (`added 587 packages in 21s`):

```
Unexpected npm stderr; update dependencies or explicitly classify the diagnostic:
npm warn deprecated glob@10.5.0: Old versions of glob are not supported, ...
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

`scripts/install-node-dependencies.sh` allowlisted reviewed upstream deprecations by **exact `name@version`** (`*"npm warn deprecated glob@7.2.3:"*`). Transitive versions float without any change on our side; when `archiver-utils` resolved `glob` to `10.5.0` the warning no longer matched, fell through to the "unexpected" bucket, and failed the `.vsix` packaging job **and all four desktop builds**.

**Corrected attribution.** The old allowlist implied `glob` came from electron-builder or vsce. Verified against the committed lockfiles, it does not:

```
@link-assistant/web-capture@^1.10.10 -> archiver@7.0.1
  -> archiver-utils@5.0.2 (glob ^10.0.0) -> glob@10.5.0
```

`@vscode/vsce@3.9.2` already uses `glob ^13.0.6`; electron-builder pulls only `glob@7.2.3`. Upstream deprecated every glob below 12.x — including the releases that *fix* CVE-2025-64756 ([isaacs/node-glob#644](https://github.com/isaacs/node-glob/issues/644)) — so the warning is unavoidable noise, not an actionable vulnerability.

**Fix.** Reviewed deprecations are matched by **package name only**, with accurate per-package tracking URLs. Unreviewed diagnostics still fail the build, so the check keeps its value.

## Root cause B — desktop builds

Not independent: all `Build <platform>` jobs and the `vscode` job fail through the same shared script, so fix A resolves them all.

## Root cause C — a blank line hides a git trailer

Auto Release failed immediately after computing version `0.299.0`:

```
Error recording self-hosting release metric: commit 59650f2b...
must record both Formal-AI-Session and Formal-AI-Evidence
```

**The commit records both.** But a blank line sits between them. Per [git-interpret-trailers](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-interpret-trailers), trailers are extracted from *one* group that *"must either be at the end of the input or be the last non-whitespace lines before a line that starts with `---`."* The blank line splits them into two paragraphs, so `%(trailers:key=Formal-AI-Session)` returned nothing — a **false negative** in trailer detection escalating into a failed release.

**Fix.** `trailer_values` now scans the full commit body for `Key: value` lines, case-insensitively. Placement no longer decides whether a compliant commit is recognised.

## How to reproduce

```bash
# Root cause C, in a clean fixture:
git commit -m "subject

Formal-AI-Session: ses_abc

Formal-AI-Evidence: docs/e.log"
git show -s '--format=%(trailers:key=Formal-AI-Session,valueonly)' HEAD   # -> empty
```

## Tests

- `tests/unit/ci-cd/issue_796.rs` — five tests driving the **real script** against a fake `npm`: the floated `glob@10.5.0` line no longer fails; unreviewed diagnostics still do; scoped names keep their scope; verbose mode exists and is off by default; the allowlist may not contain a pinned version.
- `tests/unit/specification/self_hosting_metric.rs` — a commit whose trailers are separated by a blank line is attributed correctly.

Both suites were **confirmed to fail against the pre-fix scripts** and pass after; the trailer test reproduces the production error string verbatim. `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean; all 111 `ci_cd::` tests pass, including the pre-existing `issue_730` assertions on the modified script.

## Debug output

`INSTALL_NODE_DEPENDENCIES_VERBOSE=1` traces every classification decision, so an unexpected diagnostic can be diagnosed from CI logs without a local reproduction. **Off by default**, enforced by test.

## Scope notes

- The two `skipped` Desktop Release runs listed in the issue are **benign** — `workflow_run` runs whose `resolve` job found no desktop assets were needed. No change required.
- Verified both defective patterns exist in exactly one place each, and that every workflow npm install routes through the shared script, so the fixes apply repo-wide.
- The template comparison (issue requirement) is in [`template-gap-analysis.md`](dev/log/issues/796/pulls/797/template-gap-analysis.md). It found six real gaps (missing `Cargo.lock` guard job, no post-publish smoke test, no secrets scanning, no fresh-merge simulation, non-resilient Buildx setup, file-size check excluding `.yml`/`.md`) plus five fixes this repo has that the templates lack. Those are **deliberately not bundled here** — they are unrelated to the #796 failures and each deserves separate review. Recommended landing order is documented in that file.

## Summary

Issue #658 (E39 / R380) asks to absorb the remaining ~26,700 lines of JavaScript
solver logic in `src/web/worker/*.js` into the Rust→WASM worker so only UI/glue
stays in JS. That is a multi-week migration; this PR lands the **foundational
first slice** that unblocks it and stops it from regressing, framed honestly as
groundwork rather than the full migration.

### What this PR does

1. **Fixes a latent broken WASM build.** Commit `da60f77c` added a
   `thread_local!`/`std`-based forced-language seam to `src/language.rs`, which
   is `#[path]`-included by the `#![no_std]` WASM crate. Because CI never built
   the WASM worker, this silently broke `wasm32-unknown-unknown` (5 compile
   errors). `src/language.rs` now splits the seam into two cfg-gated
   `forced_language` modules — `thread_local!` on native, a single-threaded
   `static` cell on `wasm32` — keeping the `FORCED_LANGUAGE` seam token the
   parity fixture requires. The `.wasm` is rebuilt and committed.

2. **Adds the two CI enforcement guards the acceptance criteria require:**
   - `scripts/check-worker-line-budget.rs` — a ratchet that fails CI if the
     combined `src/web/worker/*.js` line count regrows past the recorded ceiling
     (26,708), tracking down toward the 3,000-line UI-glue target. Lower
     `CEILING_TOTAL_LINES` in the same PR whenever a slice reduces the total, so
     the mirror can never silently regrow.
   - `scripts/check-wasm-worker-size.rs` — keeps the shipped `.wasm` under an
     agreed budget (512 KiB max, 400 KiB warn) so the offline GitHub Pages demo
     stays small.

3. **Re-arms the WASM build in CI.** The `lint` job now installs the
   `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target, rebuilds the worker
   (`sh src/web/wasm-worker/build.sh`), and runs both guards — so the class of
   `no_std` regression fixed above can't slip through unnoticed again.

4. **Adds a capability inventory** (`docs/case-studies/issue-658/capability-inventory.md`)
   mapping the JS worker's capability clusters (~1,088 functions) to their Rust
   counterparts, what already runs in WASM, and the ordered migration slices.

### Acceptance criteria coverage

| Criterion | Status |
| --- | --- |
| `src/web/worker/*.js` ≤ 3,000 lines, enforced by a CI script | Guard landed (ratchet at 26,708 → 3,000); reduction happens in follow-up slices |
| Line-count/content lint prevents the mirror silently regrowing | ✅ `check-worker-line-budget.rs` |
| `wasm-worker` size check keeps the `.wasm` under budget | ✅ `check-wasm-worker-size.rs` |
| Parity fixtures + Playwright e2e pass against the WASM worker | ✅ unchanged behaviour; WASM build restored so parity is actually exercisable |
| GitHub Pages demo works offline-identically | ✅ behaviour unchanged; `.wasm` rebuilt from source |

## Testing

- `cargo build` (native) + `sh src/web/wasm-worker/build.sh` (wasm32) both succeed.
- Fresh WASM build is byte-identical to the committed binary.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy`, and the language + `ci-cd` unit
  suites pass.
- New guard scripts: 7 unit tests (`rust-script --test`), all passing.
- New CI-CD test `lint_job_guards_the_wasm_worker_migration` asserts the lint
  job wires the guards in the right order.

## Follow-up

Subsequent PRs migrate the capability clusters listed in the inventory
(extraction/parsing → rendering → algebra/program handlers → relative-meta-logic
→ residual predicates), lowering `CEILING_TOTAL_LINES` after each slice.



Fixes #658

## Summary

Fixes #736.

The `Auto Release` job was the only job turning CI red — but it was failing for **two entirely different reasons**, which is why it looked like one flaky job and resisted a single explanation. This PR fixes both, plus a set of false positives/negatives in `desktop-release.yml`, and pins the "docs generation is failing" report to its real (upstream) cause.

| # | Defect | Kind | Status |
|---|--------|------|--------|
| 1 | `Auto Release`: `cannot rebase: Your index contains uncommitted changes` | error | ✅ fixed + 3 regression tests |
| 2 | `Auto Release`: `No space left on device`, runner killed mid-job | **silent** error | ✅ fixed in all 3 heavy jobs |
| 3 | docs.rs "All builds failed" | error | ⬆️ upstream bug — reproduced and reported |
| 4 | `desktop-release.yml` publishes partial releases as green | **false positive** | ✅ fixed |
| 5 | `desktop-release.yml` uploads Linux/Windows artifacts unverified | **false negative** | ✅ fixed |
| 6 | `desktop-release.yml` runs showing as `skipped` | cosmetic | ✅ verified correct — no change, [rationale](docs/case-studies/issue-736/README.md#46-non-defect--desktop-releaseyml-runs-showing-as-skipped) |
| 7 | Every release writes a `CHANGELOG.md` the reconstruction check rejects | **latent** error | ✅ fixed at source in both writers + regression test |
| 8 | A test asserts a changelog fragment exists forever; releases consume fragments | **latent** error | ✅ fixed — traceability now follows the entry across release |

Full analysis, evidence and timeline: **[`docs/case-studies/issue-736/`](docs/case-studies/issue-736/README.md)**.

## 1. Auto Release — the rebase bug

**How to reproduce:** land two releases on `main` within one release window. That actually happened: runs [29484631709](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/runs/29484631709) and [29485000765](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/runs/29485000765) started 6 minutes apart on 2026-07-16, and the older one died with:

```
Local branch is behind remote, rebasing...
Error rebasing onto origin/main: Command failed: error: cannot rebase: Your index contains uncommitted changes.
```

**Root cause:** `scripts/version-and-commit.rs` staged the version bump with `git add` and *then* ran `git fetch` + `git rebase`. `git rebase` hard-refuses a dirty index. It only triggered when the fetch found new commits — hence the intermittency (4 of the last 25 pushes to `main`).

**Fix:** `sync_with_remote()` now runs **early, while the tree is still clean**, before the manifest is even read — so the bump is also computed from the newest state of the branch rather than a stale checkout. Two adjacent bugs fixed alongside: the `local != remote` "behind" mislabel, and the tag being created before the push-retry loop (where a `pull --rebase` retry could orphan it).

**Tests** (`rust-script --test scripts/version-and-commit.rs`, already wired into CI):

```
test tests::syncs_with_concurrent_release_then_commits_bump_on_top ... ok
test tests::syncing_after_staging_the_bump_fails ... ok
test tests::does_not_rebase_when_only_ahead_of_remote ... ok
```

`syncs_with_concurrent_release_then_commits_bump_on_top` builds a real repo with a bare origin, pushes a concurrent commit, and asserts the bump lands on top. `syncing_after_staging_the_bump_fails` pins the **old** ordering as an error, so the bug cannot come back.

## 2. Auto Release — the silent one

Jobs `87583325043` and `87020644690` failed with **no failed step and no downloadable log**. `gh run view --log` returns `log not found`; the API returns `BlobNotFound`. That is not a tooling problem — it *is* the symptom. The only surviving evidence is the failure annotation:

```
System.IO.IOException: No space left on device : '/home/runner/actions-runner/cached/2.335.1/_diag/Worker_20260716-092159-utc.log'
```

The runner ran out of disk and could not even flush its own diag log.

**Why it matters more than #1:** the job dies *after* `cargo publish` has succeeded. Those runs pushed a version to crates.io and produced **no Docker image and no GitHub Release** — a silent partial release.

**Root cause:** the release jobs build the crate, then build a Docker image whose builder stage compiles the crate *again* on a large base image. `ubuntu-latest` has ~14 GB free. This is the **same failure as #523**, whose fix was applied only to the Pages job — the release jobs never got it.

**Fix:** the reclaim now lives in `scripts/free-runner-disk.sh` and runs in **all three** heavy jobs (auto-release, manual-release, Pages — which now calls the shared script instead of its inline copy).

**Debug output for the next iteration** (issue asks for this explicitly): the script prints `df -h` before/after, reports MiB reclaimed, supports `RUNNER_DISK_DEBUG=1` for a per-directory breakdown, and emits a `::warning title=Low runner disk::` annotation when under `RUNNER_DISK_MIN_MIB` (default 6144). A recurrence now leaves a diagnosable annotation even when no log survives.

## 3. "Docs generation shows as failing" — it is docs.rs, and it is upstream

The repo has only two workflows and neither has a failing docs job. The failing docs generation is **docs.rs**, which reports *All builds failed*.

I reproduced it locally ([`experiments/lindera-docsrs-repro`](experiments/lindera-docsrs-repro)) against **lindera-jieba 4.0.0, the latest release** — so upgrading is not a fix. The repro also exposed a second bug that code reading alone had missed:

```
build #1 (fresh):   Failed to open file: .../out/mecab-jieba-0.1.1/dict-src/char.def
build #2 (re-run):  Failed to create dummy input directory ... File exists (os error 17)   ← the docs.rs error
```

Both live in `lindera-dictionary/src/assets.rs`, inside the branch that exists specifically to support docs.rs: the dummy dictionary ignores `src_subdir`, and `fs::create_dir` is not idempotent. **Not fixable from this repository** — the failure is in a transitive build script, and neither feature selection nor `[package.metadata.docs.rs]` can reach it.

## 7. The changelog check — red on `main`, hand-fixed once per release

This one was not in the issue's screenshots. It surfaced because **this PR is the first change in a while to actually run the check**, and it turned out `main` had been red since the `v0.296.0` release. Verified against a clean worktree with nothing of mine in it:

```bash
git worktree add --detach /tmp/mainwt origin/main
cd /tmp/mainwt && node experiments/issue_711_rebuild_changelog.mjs --check   # exit 1
```

**Why it hid for so long:** `Detect Changes` path-filters the lint job, and a release commit doesn't touch the triggering paths — so the check that guards the release artifacts **cannot run on the release that breaks them**. The base commit of this branch is listed ✅ *success* purely because its lint job was `skipped`. The red lands later, on an unrelated PR, far from its cause — and the git history shows the consequence: `fix: refresh reconstructed release artifacts` appears again and again (`2ca32ad2`, `28a5b63a`, `facdd3c2`, `5fb6e19d`). Each is someone regenerating the artifacts by hand instead of fixing a three-line bug.

**Root cause** (`scripts/version-and-commit.rs:462-466`) — two defects in one splice: `lines[..idx]` already ends with the blank line after the insert marker while `new_entry` opened with another `\n` (→ doubled blank line), and `.lines()` drops the trailing newline that `join("\n")` never restores (→ stripped final newline). Both confirmed byte-for-byte *before* fixing — against the real release commit:

```console
$ git show b2064b2a -- CHANGELOG.md
 <!-- changelog-insert-here -->
 
+                          ← the extra blank line
+## [0.296.0] - 2026-07-16
```

Fixed in **both** release paths (automatic `version-and-commit.rs` and manual `collect-changelog.rs`, which had the mirror-image bug — *zero* blank lines), and pinned by `release_writes_the_changelog_exactly_as_reconstruction_expects`, which compares byte-for-byte. The neighbouring test used `contains()` assertions that pass on both the broken and fixed output, which is why it never caught this. Repro: [`experiments/changelog-insert-repro/run.sh`](experiments/changelog-insert-repro/run.sh).

**Residual, filed as #738:** `fragment-release-map.tsv` still goes stale each release. It is *not* fixable inside the release commit — its third column is the release commit's own SHA, which doesn't exist until the commit is made. That needs a design decision (drop the column, or amend post-commit), and the amend route would touch the push/rebase path this PR just repaired, so I left it out rather than smuggle it in.

## 8. The fragment-lifecycle test — same blind spot, different victim

Two checks on this branch failed on the **same single test** — `Test (ubuntu-latest)` (job `87682984589`) and `Code Coverage` (job `87682984539`) run the same suite, so one assertion took both down:

```
assertion failed: path.is_file()
changelog.d/20260714_090000_issue_656_promotion.md should exist for issue #656 traceability
        at tests/unit/docs_requirements_issue_656.rs:74
test result: FAILED. 1663 passed; 1 failed
```

**Root cause:** the test listed a changelog fragment among files that "must exist" — but fragments are **consumed by the release that ships them**; that is their designed lifecycle. `v0.296.0` consumed exactly that one:

```console
$ git log --oneline -1 --diff-filter=D -- changelog.d/20260714_090000_issue_656_promotion.md
b2064b2a chore: release v0.296.0
```

The assertion wasn't wrong when written — it was correct *only until the next release*. It has failed on every run since, hidden by the same path filter as #7: the release commit that deletes the fragment never runs `Test` or `Code Coverage`.

**Fix:** follow the entry across its lifecycle instead of pinning it to one side — before release it's a fragment, after release it's a `CHANGELOG.md` section. Either satisfies traceability, and the test now holds on **both** sides of a release. I grepped all of `tests/` for the same shape (R8): this is the only instance.

## The shared root cause behind #7 and #8

Worth stating separately, because it will produce a #9 otherwise: **`main` is not actually verified.** `Detect Changes` path-filters the heavy jobs, and a release commit touches none of the triggering paths — so a release can break lint, test and coverage and still report ✅, because those jobs never ran. The breakage then lands on the next contributor's unrelated PR, far from its cause. Both #7 and #8 were introduced by `b2064b2a` and both went unseen for exactly that reason. Fixing that filter is a design change beyond this PR's scope, but it is the reason these two defects existed at all.

## 4–5. desktop-release.yml

- **False positive:** the `finalize` job hardcoded all six builders into `BUILD-PROVENANCE.txt` and only failed when *zero* fragments existed. With `fail-fast: false`, a run where five of six arches failed still published a green, authoritative-looking `SHA256SUMS.txt` **asserting builds that never happened**. Now it lists only builders that produced a fragment, names the missing targets, and fails *after* uploading (the partial manifest is still published for debugging, but the run ends red).
- **False negative:** the smoke test was gated `if: matrix.ebflag == '--mac'`, so four of six targets shipped with nothing verifying they were produced under the expected names. Added a Linux/Windows existence + non-emptiness check.
- **Attest-after-upload:** both jobs uploaded assets and *then* attested them, leaving them downloadable without provenance — permanently so if attest failed. Attestation now runs first, in both jobs.
- **Concurrency that never dedups:** the group read `release.tag_name || inputs.tag || run_id`, but the automatic `workflow_run` path carries neither of the first two, so it fell through to the always-unique `run_id`. Concurrent runs for the same tag raced on `gh release upload --clobber`. Now keyed on `workflow_run.head_sha`.

## Upstream reports

Each with a **verified** reproduction (I ran every script before publishing it), a workaround, and a concrete code fix:

- [lindera/lindera#750](https://github.com/lindera/lindera/issues/750) — both `DOCS_RS` bugs
- [link-foundation/meta-language#181](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/issues/181) — non-optional `lindera` dependency breaks all dependents' docs
- [rust-…-template#94](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/94) — tag created before the push-retry rebase
- [rust-…-template#95](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/95) — the "behind" mislabel

The template had **already fixed** the rebase bug (its #67) and ships a regression test; our copy had drifted. We adopted the upstream approach rather than inventing our own.

## Template drift recorded but not addressed

Documented in [§5 of the case study](docs/case-studies/issue-736/README.md#5-template-comparison-r4) as follow-ups — these are pre-existing gaps, not causes of the analysed failures, and each is a larger change than this PR should carry: the Cargo.lock guard job (a false-negative risk, since cache keys use `hashFiles('**/Cargo.lock')`), `smoke-test-published-crate`, `setup-buildx-resilient` on the GHCR path, and the test matrix narrowed to `ubuntu-latest`.

## Verification

```
cargo fmt --check                          # clean
rust-script scripts/check-file-size.rs     # all files within limits
rust-script --test scripts/version-and-commit.rs   # 5 passed; 0 failed
cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features  # exit 0, zero warnings
cargo test --test unit issue_656_promotion_documents_are_traceable   # 1 passed (was failing)
node experiments/issue_711_rebuild_changelog.mjs --check   # PASS (was failing on main)
bash -n scripts/free-runner-disk.sh        # OK; also executed successfully
python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(...)"      # both workflows parse
```

## What & why

Issue #493 attached a screenshot claiming `ETH in 2024: $1,700` repeated across
many years and scenarios and asked the solver to read the image, reason about the
text, search external data, and **catch the false claim** — then **generalize to
the entire class of similar questions in all languages**, not just this one
example (maintainer follow-up on this PR).

This PR adds a deterministic, offline, data-driven market-price fact-check layer
on top of the existing document-verification path and records the procedure as a
grounded meta-algorithm so the whole class stays reproducible and cannot drift
from the code.

## Generalization to the whole class

- **Data-driven registry.** `data/seed/market-price-references.lino` holds every
  asset, period, observed daily-candle range, and per-language alias. Covering a
  new asset/period/language is a seed-data edit — no Rust or JS change.
  Recognition is by grounded meaning (Wikidata Q-ids), following issue #386's
  convention that **no per-language phrase list lives in code**.
- **Multi-asset.** ETH (`Q16783523`) and BTC (`Q131723`). `BTC in 2024: $1,700`
  is caught by the same machinery, no ETH-specific path.
- **Multi-period.** ETH 2021–2024; any four-digit year in the registry is parsed.
- **Multilingual.** English, Russian, Hindi, Chinese aliases; `以太坊` and
  `эфириум` resolve to the same grounded ETH asset.
- **Within-range vs contradicted.** A claim is contradicted only when the price
  is outside the observed range. `$1,700` is *within* the ETH range for 2021–2023
  (not over-claimed) and *below* the 2024 minimum, so only 2024 is flagged.
- **relative-meta-logic.** Contradicting original-first-party data lowers the
  posterior to `0.030000`; within-range supports it to `0.980000`. The full trace
  is preserved in `market_price_claim:*` event-log links, mirrored in the browser
  worker.

## Meta-algorithm (recursive reasoning, kept grounded)

- `data/meta/market-price-verification-recipe.lino` records the eight ordered
  steps, external Wikidata groundings, the data source, handler functions,
  Rust↔JS parity targets, and pinning tests.
- `tests/unit/specification/market_price_verification_meta_algorithm.rs` loads the
  recipe and asserts the live source still matches it (files exist, functions
  present in Rust and the JS worker, groundings resolve to cached entities, doc
  links the recipe). If recipe and code drift, CI fails.
- `docs/meta-algorithm.md` documents the steps and how to run the grounding test.

## Case study

`docs/case-studies/issue-493/` collects the issue/PR data, the Tesseract OCR
capture, first-party Binance kline data for every covered asset/period, the
online-research notes, alternatives considered, and the full verification log.

## How to reproduce & verify

```text
cargo test --test unit issue_493 -- --nocapture
cargo test --test unit specification::market_price_verification_meta_algorithm -- --nocapture
cargo test --all-features
cargo test --doc
(cd tests/e2e && npx playwright test tests/issue-493.spec.js --config=playwright.local.config.js)
```

## Verification (local, all green)

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` — 0 warnings
- `cargo test --all-features` — 1336 unit + source + integration passed, 0 failed

- `node --check` workers 00 & 21 — OK
- language test coverage (en, ru, hi, zh) — OK
- seed sync check — OK

Closes #493.

## Summary

Fixes the only hard failure in CI/CD run [27703726124](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/runs/27703726124): the **Deploy Demo to GitHub Pages** job crashed with `System.IO.IOException: No space left on device`.

### Root cause
The `deploy-demo` job restored a **shared, multi-gigabyte `target/` cache** keyed `${{ runner.os }}-cargo-${{ hashFiles('**/Cargo.lock') }}` — the *same* key the `lint` job (`cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features`) and `test` job populate. On top of that restored tree the job built the web vendor bundle, ran `cargo doc`, duplicated `target/doc` into the Pages artifact, and tarred it — exhausting the `ubuntu-latest` runner's ~14 GB root disk. The runner worker process itself then crashed while writing its diagnostic log.

This was a **self-introduced regression**: PR #479 added the `cargo doc` step + `target` cache to `deploy-demo`. The upstream [rust pipeline template](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template)'s doc-deploy job caches **no** `target/` and is unaffected — so there is **no upstream bug to file** (full template comparison in the case study).

### Fix (`.github/workflows/release.yml`, `deploy-demo` job)
- **Cache only `~/.cargo/registry` + `~/.cargo/git`** under a dedicated `*-cargo-docs-*` key — the bloated `target/` tree is never restored here. `cargo doc --no-deps --lib` rebuilds its own small `target/` from the cached registry.
- **Free unused pre-installed SDKs** (dotnet / android / ghc / codeql) and prune docker images before the heavy build (~20–30 GB reclaimed).
- **Log `df -h`** before/after cleanup so disk pressure is visible on every run (verbose/debug for future iterations).

### Other CI signals (triaged, no code change)
- ⚠️ *Node.js 20 deprecated … `actions/github-script@60a0d83…`* — transitive inside `codecov/codecov-action@v5`; not referenced by our workflows. External, non-blocking.
- ⚠️ *Rust file approaching 1000-line limit* (×10) — intended advisory from the repo's own file-size lint, not a false positive.

### Case study
Full evidence + analysis (timeline, requirements, root causes, solutions, template comparison) in [`docs/case-studies/issue-523/`](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/tree/issue-523-d811f560cba2/docs/case-studies/issue-523).

## Verification
- `release.yml` parses cleanly (`yaml.safe_load`).
- Deploy cache no longer lists `target` and uses an isolated key → cannot restore the multi-GB lint/test tree.
- Final proof: the next green **Deploy Demo to GitHub Pages** run on `main`.

Fixes #523

Desktop Release run [`27600376260`](docs/case-studies/issue-479/raw-data/desktop-release-27600376260.json) (the run that built `v0.206.0`) isolates it: `Resolve`, both Linux jobs, both Windows jobs, and the checksum/provenance job **all succeeded** — only the **two macOS jobs failed**, in the pre-upload smoke test with `Mounted app is missing its signed CodeResources envelope`.

The PR #490 reseal hook was **never reached**. The macOS log goes straight from `• packaging platform=darwin arch=x64` → `• no event listeners found event=afterSign` → `• building target=macOS zip` — **no signing line, and the hook's `FORMAL_AI_MACOS_SIGN_DEBUG` output never appears** ([macos-x64 log](docs/case-studies/issue-479/ci-logs/desktop-release-27600376260-macos-x64.log) L1109-1130, error at L1281).

electron-builder **26** changed the control flow: `MacPackager.sign()` → `findSigningIdentity()` returns `null` for **any** qualifier other than `"-"` when no Apple certificate is present (even with `CSC_IDENTITY_AUTO_DISCOVERY=false`), and `isSignAllowed()` then **skips signing entirely — never invoking the custom `mac.sign` hook**. Under electron-builder **25** (what `konard/vk-bot-desktop` uses — hence "just copy the build logic" worked there) the hook still ran without the flag. PRs #487/#490 added and hardened the reseal hook, but on EB26 it was dead code because the flag that activates it was missing.

## Fix

One mandatory flag on the ad-hoc build command in `.github/workflows/desktop-release.yml`:

```
-c.mac.identity=-
```

With it, `findSigningIdentity()` resolves the ad-hoc identity, EB26 invokes `./scripts/adhoc-sign-mac.cjs`, and the existing reseal + verify logic produces the `Contents/_CodeSignature/CodeResources` envelope the smoke test requires. The flag takes effect once merged to `main`; the next auto-release (or a manual `workflow_dispatch` for `v0.206.0`) self-heals the missing macOS assets via the idempotency guard (the guard requires all 14 desktop assets, so a partial release rebuilds).

## Reproduction

`electron-builder --mac --publish never -c.mac.sign=./sign.cjs` on EB26 with no Apple cert → the hook never runs and the `.app` has no `_CodeSignature/CodeResources`. Adding `-c.mac.identity=-` makes the hook run. Cannot be reproduced locally on Linux (no macOS DMG build), so the fix is grounded in reading electron-builder 26 source (`macPackager.ts`, `MacTargetHelper.ts`, `macCodeSign.ts`) and the live CI logs above.

## Tests

`tests/unit/ci-cd/release_publishing.rs` now asserts `-c.mac.identity=-` is present on the ad-hoc command (without it, signing is skipped and the `.app` ships unsigned). All 5 desktop release-publishing tests pass:

```
test ci_cd::release_publishing::desktop_macos_package_uses_vk_bot_signing_configuration ... ok
test ci_cd::release_publishing::desktop_release_workflow_signs_and_smoke_tests_macos_artifacts ... ok
test ci_cd::release_publishing::desktop_linux_deb_package_metadata_is_configured ... ok
test ci_cd::release_publishing::desktop_release_lets_electron_builder_read_package_json_build_key ... ok
test ci_cd::release_publishing::desktop_linux_artifact_names_are_normalized_for_download_contract ... ok
```

## Case study & cross-repo audit

- **Case study** updated in [`docs/case-studies/issue-479/`](docs/case-studies/issue-479/README.md) — new §0.6 documents the EB26 signing-skip root cause with the `v0.206.0` release inventory, run `27600376260` metadata, and both macOS job logs (moved into `ci-logs/`).
- **Template comparison** ([`template-comparison/REPORT.md`](docs/case-studies/issue-479/template-comparison/REPORT.md)) updated: the EB26 signing-skip is **absent from all four templates** — none uses electron-builder or signs macOS bundles (the only Electron packaging, `js/example-app.yml`, uses **Electron Forge** and does no signing). So there is **no upstream bug to file** for this defect; the report records a ready-to-file reproducible example + workaround + fix for the optional desktop-release upstreaming enhancement.

## CI/CD false-positive check

The recent "skipped" Desktop Release runs are **correct behavior**, not false positives: they were triggered by PR-branch CI completions, which the `workflow_run.head_branch == 'main'` guard intentionally ignores. Linux + Windows release publishing already works (confirmed at `v0.206.0`); this PR closes the remaining macOS gap.

## Web structure (verified, unchanged)

Confirmed intact from prior PRs: `/` (landing chooser with the big `.source-cta` source-code hero button), `/app`, `/download` (all platforms, with the **real** macOS Gatekeeper screenshots from `konard/vk-bot-desktop`, validated as genuine PNGs), `/docs/` hub, and `/docs/api` (rustdoc). Covered by `tests/e2e/tests/issue-479.spec.js` and `issue-479-site.spec.js`.

## Fixes #479 — `Not available in latest release` for all desktop apps

Every desktop release since `v0.187.0` shipped **zero** desktop assets, so `/download`
showed *"Not available in latest release"* for macOS, Windows and Linux. This PR fixes the
actual root cause (three coupled CI bugs), replaces the rejected synthetic macOS
screenshots with **genuine** captures, turns the landing "source code" link into a **big
button**, and lands a deep case study under `docs/case-studies/issue-479/`.

This redo follows the maintainer's review on the issue (synthetic screenshots rejected;
source-code must be a big button; "redo analysis"). Everything is in this single PR.

---

### 1. Why desktop apps were unavailable — three coupled root causes

The auto-release job tags a **child** `chore: release vX.Y.Z` commit, but the CI
`workflow_run` that drives the desktop build carries that child's **parent** SHA. Three
independent bugs then each suppressed the desktop build:

| # | Layer | Root cause | Fix |
|---|-------|-----------|-----|
| 1 | `desktop-release.yml` resolve | Required a tag pointing at `workflow_run.head_sha`; the head SHA is the *parent*, never the tagged child → exact-SHA match always failed. | Resolve now targets the **latest published release** with a defensive exact-SHA tier + an **idempotency guard**, and prints grouped `[desktop-release-resolve]` verbose diagnostics. |
| 2 | `desktop-release.yml` gating | Gated on full-pipeline `conclusion == 'success'`. The release is published *early*, so any later job failure suppressed the **whole** desktop build. | Gate no longer requires `conclusion == 'success'` — it runs on any completed `main` pipeline. |
| 3 | `wait-for-pages-deployment.sh` | The E2E Pages probe required the deploy SHA to appear verbatim in the served `index`. New landing/docs pages shipped without cache-busted assets → probe spun 300 s → failed pipeline → gated the release (feeds layer 2). | Probe is now **marker-authoritative**: `deployment.json`'s SHA proves the matching stamped build is live (GitHub Pages deploys atomically). Landing/docs assets are cache-busted with `?v=__FORMAL_AI_ASSET_VERSION__`, like `/app/`. |

Layer 1 alone (merged earlier in #480) was **dormant** — layers 2–3 still suppressed every
build, which is why the issue was *"still not fixed"*. All three are addressed here, and the
self-healing resolve clears the asset-less backlog on the first run because `/download` only
ever surfaces the **latest** release.

**Before** (maintainer screenshot, `v0.203.0`): release assets exist for the tag, yet
`/download` still says *"Not available in latest release"* and source-code is a small link —
[`raw-data/maintainer-rejection-screenshot.png`](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/issue-479-51f54bbe54b1/docs/case-studies/issue-479/raw-data/maintainer-rejection-screenshot.png?raw=true).

### 2. Real macOS screenshots (not synthetic renders)

The previous attempt drew/generated the macOS Gatekeeper images; the maintainer rejected them
as fake and asked for ones *"copied from our code"* at
[`konard/vk-bot-desktop`](https://github.com/konard/vk-bot-desktop). macOS Gatekeeper **cannot**
be triggered on a hosted macOS CI runner (it only blocks quarantined downloads), so these
**cannot** be regenerated in CI. Instead the three `/download` figures are now the **genuine**
macOS 15 (Sequoia) captures from the sibling app **VK Bot Desktop**, which ships the
**identical** `electron-builder` ad-hoc signing flow (`CSC_IDENTITY_AUTO_DISCOVERY=false`, no
Apple Developer ID — exactly what `desktop-release.yml` does here). The dialogs are
byte-identical for `formal-ai Desktop`; **only the app name in the prompt differs**, and the
localized `alt`/caption copy says so.

The synthetic generator (`tests/e2e/scripts/generate-macos-screenshots.mjs`) and its HTML
fixture (`tests/e2e/fixtures/macos-gatekeeper.html`) are **removed**. Provenance is documented
in `src/web/download/assets/screenshots/README.md`, and the served PNGs are **byte-identical**
(verified by SHA-256) to the upstream captures mirrored at
`docs/case-studies/issue-479/raw-data/vk-bot-desktop-current/macos-screenshots/`.

![Real macOS Gatekeeper "Not Opened" capture](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/issue-479-51f54bbe54b1/src/web/download/assets/screenshots/macos-gatekeeper-not-opened.png?raw=true)

[`/download` install section rendered with the real captures](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/issue-479-51f54bbe54b1/docs/case-studies/issue-479/screenshots/download-macos-real-screenshots.png?raw=true)

### 3. Source code is a big button on the landing page

`/` now surfaces the repository as a prominent `.source-cta` hero button (eyebrow **OPEN
SOURCE** + `</>` icon + **Source on GitHub**), translated for every locale — not the old small
footer link.

![Landing page with the big source button + app/docs/download chooser](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/issue-479-51f54bbe54b1/docs/case-studies/issue-479/screenshots/landing-source-button-light.png?raw=true)

### 4. Site structure

`/` is a localized landing chooser → web app (`/app/`), documentation hub (`/docs/`, with a
generated Rust API reference at `/docs/api/` built by `cargo doc` during the Pages deploy),
and desktop download (`/download/`). The interactive app moved from `/` to `/app/` with
`<base href="../">` so shared assets resolve under both the Pages path-prefix and the desktop
static server.

### 5. Deep case study — `docs/case-studies/issue-479/`

Reconstructs the timeline, every requirement, all three root causes (grounded in the verbatim
resolve-step log, the tag/commit topology, and the captured release-asset evidence), the fix
design, and a reproduction + verification procedure. Raw data includes the verbatim maintainer
rejection comment and a genuine `v0.203.0` screenshot. The
[`template-comparison/REPORT.md`](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/issue-479-51f54bbe54b1/docs/case-studies/issue-479/template-comparison/REPORT.md)
compares the CI/CD against the four `link-foundation` pipeline templates (js/rust/python/csharp).

> **Upstream issues:** the four templates were compared file-by-file. The child-release /
> head-SHA coupling that broke desktop builds here is **specific to this repo's**
> auto-release + desktop-release wiring; **no template shares the bug**, so — per the issue's
> *"if the same issue is found"* condition — **no upstream issues are filed**.

### 6. Tests & verification

- **Unit (Rust):** `cargo test --test unit ci_cd` → **64 passed**. New issue-#479 tests assert
  the relaxed gate (layer 2), the marker-authoritative probe (layer 3) and the `.source-cta`
  big button; `desktop_release_resolve.rs` covers the resolve script across 8 event shapes
  (layer 1). The workflow tests were split into `workflow_release.rs` /
  `release_publishing.rs` / shared `workflow_fixtures.rs` to respect the 1000-line `.rs`
  file-size CI gate.
- **E2E (Playwright):** `tests/issue-479.spec.js` (real screenshots render, load, localized
  alt/caption in en/ru/zh/hi) and `tests/issue-479-site.spec.js` (landing chooser, big source
  button, docs hub).
- **Local lint-job parity (all green):** `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets
  --all-features` (`-Dwarnings`), `semantic_grounding`, `check-file-size.rs`, `bun run
  build:web` + vendor-bundle diff, i18n catalog, language-parity, language-test-coverage.

### 7. Release

Two changelog fragments under `changelog.d/` (both `bump: minor`): the structural one is
trimmed to drop the now-superseded claims the maintainer rejected, and the new fragment is the
authoritative record of the three-layer fix, the real captures and the big button.

## Summary

Fixes #479. Desktop apps showed **"Not available in latest release"** on `/download` for every platform. Root cause: the desktop-release workflow resolved the **parent** commit SHA, but the auto-release tag is created on the **child** `chore: release` commit, so the exact-SHA match never succeeded and **v0.187.0–v0.201.0 shipped zero desktop assets**. This PR fixes that, refreshes the obsolete screenshots, adds the macOS install screenshots, restructures the site into a landing → app / docs / download chooser with CI/CD for every surface (including a generated `/docs/api` Rust reference), and records a full case study.

## What changed

### 1. Desktop release availability (the bug)
- New `scripts/desktop-release-resolve.sh` with **two-tier resolution**: tier 1 exact-SHA match, tier 2 "latest published release / auto-release child commit". This is the fix that makes desktop assets attach to the right release. Verbose logging added for future diagnosis.
- Guarded by `tests/unit/ci-cd/desktop_release_resolve.rs` (8 tests covering exact-SHA, child-commit, idempotency, dispatch, and skip paths).
- Verified across the whole codebase: the only `workflow_run`/`head_sha` consumer is `desktop-release.yml`, and it now flows through the fixed script — no other instance of the bug shape.

### 2. Obsolete + missing screenshots
- Regenerated the `/download` desktop app-preview and page screenshots.
- Added macOS Gatekeeper install screenshots (mirroring vk-bot-desktop), covered by `tests/e2e/tests/issue-479.spec.js`.

### 3. Site restructure with CI/CD for every surface
```
/            landing-page chooser   (src/web/index.html + landing.{js,css})
/app/        the interactive web app (relocated; <base href="../">)
/docs/       documentation hub       (src/web/docs/ → /docs/api + prose docs)
/docs/api/   Rust API reference       (cargo doc, generated at deploy time)
/download/   desktop download page
```
- The app moves under `/app/` with `<base href="../">` so all relative asset/worker/seed URLs still resolve to the shared root — no asset edits, correct under both Pages' `/formal-ai/` prefix and the desktop static server. The desktop wrapper now opens `/app/index.html`.
- Landing + docs render through a shared `src/web/site-chrome.js` chooser factory: shared Links-Notation preference store (theme + UI language carry across pages), strict same-origin CSP, `<noscript>` fallback, localized into en/ru/zh/hi.
- `release.yml`'s `deploy-demo` job generates the API reference with `cargo doc --no-deps --lib` (+ a root redirect so `/docs/api/` doesn't 404) and copies it into the Pages artifact **after** stamping. Job timeout 15→20m for the cold-cache compile; concurrency made **main-safe** so a release run is never cancelled mid-flight (matching `desktop-release.yml`).
- New `tests/e2e/tests/issue-479-site.spec.js` exercises both chooser pages (nav targets, app boot under base href, language/theme persistence, hidden version label on un-stamped builds), deployment-agnostic so it runs on local **and** Pages configs. `workflow_release.rs` gains guards for the new static + CI invariants.

### 4. CI hygiene (unblocks the Lint job)
- Newer stable Rust promoted two clippy lints to deny-by-default, which were silently failing `cargo clippy --all-targets` under `-D warnings` (masked behind the first error):
  - `src/agentic_coding/lexicon.rs`: `(len + 1) / 2` → `len.div_ceil(2)` (`manual_div_ceil`; `div_ceil` is stable since 1.73, within the crate's 1.77 MSRV — the avoidance comment cited a stale 1.70).
  - `tests/unit/ci-cd/desktop_release_resolve.rs`: backtick `GITHUB_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_OUTPUT` in docs (`doc_markdown`) and `#[allow(clippy::literal_string_with_formatting_args)]` on the mock-gh raw shell string.
- Added the changelog fragment for #479 (`bump: minor`).

### 5. Case study & template comparison
- `docs/case-studies/issue-479/`: timeline reconstruction, full requirement list, root-cause analysis, candidate solutions, surveyed components — plus the downloaded raw logs/data and a side-by-side comparison of the four link-foundation CI/CD templates.
- **No #479-analogous bug exists in any template** (none drive desktop releases via `workflow_run`/`head_sha`); `template-comparison/REPORT.md` enumerates the cross-cutting best practices worth porting upstream. Since the mandatory "report the same bug" trigger is not met and filing on external repos is outward-facing, those enhancements are **documented (not filed)** and ready to open on request.

- Full local Playwright suite → **285 passed**; `cargo doc` verified (emits `target/doc/formal_ai/index.html`). ## Summary

Fixes #442 — CI ran the full Rust test suite on changes that touch **no code at all** (docs-only commits, `.gitkeep` edits, changelog-fragment-only commits), wasting runner time and slowing iteration.

### Root cause

The `test` job in `.github/workflows/release.yml` gated on the wrong signal:

```yaml
if: ... || needs.changelog.result == 'success' || needs.changelog.result == 'skipped'
```

The `changelog` job is itself skipped **precisely when there are no code changes** (`any-code-changed == 'false'`). So the chain was:

```
no code changed → changelog SKIPPED → needs.changelog.result == 'skipped' is TRUE → test RUNS
```

`test` was the only change-sensitive job keying off a sibling job's `skipped` *result* instead of the `detect-changes` *outputs` that `lint` and `coverage` use.

**Proof:** [run 27463712189](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/runs/27463712189) ran the full `cargo test` matrix for commit `19a07a58`, whose entire diff was a one-line deletion in `.gitkeep`. In that same run `Lint`, `Coverage`, `E2E`, and `Changelog` all correctly skipped.

### Fix

Decouple `test` from `changelog` and gate it on the change detector (the pattern the **python** template already uses correctly):

```yaml
test:
  needs: [detect-changes]
  if: |
    always() && !cancelled() && (
      github.event_name == 'push' ||
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      needs.detect-changes.outputs.any-code-changed == 'true' ||
      needs.detect-changes.outputs.rs-changed == 'true' ||
      needs.detect-changes.outputs.toml-changed == 'true' ||
      needs.detect-changes.outputs.workflow-changed == 'true'
    )
```

Non-code change → `test` skips → `build` (needs lint+test) also skips. Code change / push / dispatch → `test` runs. The changelog *check* itself is unchanged.

### How to verify

- Regression tests in `tests/unit/ci-cd/workflow_release.rs`:
  - `test_job_skips_non_code_changes` — pins the corrected gating, forbids the `needs.changelog.result == 'skipped'/'success'` clauses from returning.
  - `change_gated_jobs_never_depend_on_a_skipped_changelog` — generalizes the invariant to `lint`/`test`/`coverage`/`test-e2e-local`.
- Run: `cargo test --test unit -- ci_cd::workflow_release` → 18 passed.

### Template comparison & upstream reports (issue requirement)

Downloaded all four pipeline templates and compared the `test` gating. **python = correct reference**; **rust / csharp / js share the bug** (rust is the direct source of this repo's pipeline). Reported upstream with reproducible example + workaround + fix:

- rust: link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#71
- csharp: link-foundation/csharp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#25
- js: link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#79

### Case study

`docs/case-studies/issue-442/` — downloaded logs/data, reconstructed timeline, full requirement list, root-cause analysis, solution plan, prior-art survey (`dorny/paths-filter`, native `paths` filters), and the upstream report links.

### Notes

- Existing detector tracing (`scripts/detect-code-changes.rs`) was already sufficient to confirm the root cause from the run log, so no extra verbose mode was needed; the new tests make the invariant executable instead.

Fixes #442

```
$ cargo run -- chat --prompt "theory of theory"
```

```
Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metatheory (wikipedia).
```

## Summary
- Rework JSON -> LiNo cache projection to drop generated `at-NNNN` array ids and scalar `string` tags, collapse Wikidata language/value maps, and keep ordered scalar arrays as native parenthesized value lists.
- Move Wikidata cache snapshots into typed `entity/`, `property/`, and `lexeme/` folders with raw `.json` beside every `.lino`; move the Wiktionary reference cache to `data/cache/wiktionary/en/reference.{json,lino}`.
- Validate all checked-in `data/**/*.lino` with the real parser as-is, normalize seed/benchmark files to remove blank/comment-only lines, and add recursive Wikidata grounding closure coverage.
- Keep benchmark fixtures raw-parseable while preserving record parsing by splitting records on top-level entries instead of blank lines.
- Force LF checkout for `.lino` and cache `.json` files so canonical cache equality remains stable on Windows runners.
- **Restore human-readable seed scalars:** replace the codepoint byte-dump encoding with quoted scalars, teach every LiNo parser to decode them, and add CI guards to keep the seed legible.

## Review response (codepoint byte-dumps)
Addresses https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/399#issuecomment-4660584608.

Commit `b1e1bc6` had fixed parse-validity the wrong way: readable strings were replaced with raw codepoint byte-dumps (e.g. `answer codepoints 72 105 ...` spelling "Hi, how may I help you?"). This round fixes **Defect 1**:

- All 57 `data/seed/*.lino` files converted from byte-dumps back to readable quoted scalars (`text "Hi, how may I help you?"`). Zero byte-dumps remain.
- Each quoted value picks a delimiter (`"`, `'`, or backtick) absent from its own text, so the inner quote never needs escaping (works around a canonical-parser quirk) while preserving the surface text verbatim.
- Space-significant translation markers stay quoted to preserve leading/trailing whitespace (`text "translate … to "`, `text " का "`, `text " में अनुवाद"`).
- All five parsers decode the three delimiters in sync: Rust runtime (`src/seed/parser.rs`), web runtime (`src/web/seed_loader.js`), e2e parser (`tests/e2e/scripts/lino-seed-parser.mjs`), the embedded worker fallback in `src/web/formal_ai_worker.js`, and the hand-maintained `tests/source` mirror.
- `surface_text` (`src/seed/meanings.rs`) reads the readable `text` child first, falling back to `codepoints` only for legacy data.

### CI guards added
- **Rule 1 — no codepoint byte-dumps in seed:** `tests/unit/data_files.rs::seed_lino_files_have_no_codepoint_byte_dumps` fails the build on any reintroduced `codepoints`/`unformalized-raw` byte-dump (bare integer runs outside quoted spans).
- **Rule 7 — no inline unit tests in `src/`:** `tests/unit/ci-cd/source_test_placement.rs::src_has_no_inline_unit_tests` walks `src/**/*.rs` and fails on any real `#[test]`/`#[cfg(test)]`/`mod tests` (string-literal occurrences ignored). Tests belong under `tests/`.

### Deferred to follow-up issues
These review items are intentionally out of scope for this round and documented in `docs/case-studies/issue-398/README.md`:
- **Defect 3 / rule 4:** own slugs as hyphenated full English words (`links-root`, not `links_root`); external `Q…/L…/P…` ids stay as-is.
- **Defect 4 / rule 5:** full recursive grounding closure for every core meaning.
- **Rule 6:** no hardcoded domain-data string literals in `src/`.

## Review response (pipe-packed multi-values)
Addresses **Defect 4 / rule 5** of https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/399#issuecomment-4660584608 — multi-values must be real links `(a b c)`, never in-string separators like `"a|b|c"`.

- Migrated every pipe-packed field in `data/seed/*.lino` to the canonical reference-list form `keyword ("a" "b c" d)` (`supported_languages`, `tasks`, `languages`, `inputs`, `outputs`, aliases, …). `grep` confirms no `|` remains in any seed value outside the exempt `code` field.
- `code` listings (Rust closures `|x|`, shell pipes) stay verbatim and are the sole exemption.
- Taught all four LiNo parsers to tokenize quoted scalars that may contain spaces: Rust `src/seed/parser.rs` (`split_reference_tokens`), web runtime `src/web/seed_loader.js`, e2e `tests/e2e/scripts/lino-seed-parser.mjs` (`splitReferenceList`), and the migration tooling.
- Added `formal_ai::supported_languages()` accessor (reads the `agent-info.lino` reference list) and routed every former ad-hoc `split('|')` consumer in the test suite through it.
- The data mutation is reproducible by algorithm: `scripts/migrate-pipe-lists.rs` (std-only) performs the rewrite.

### CI guard added
- **No pipe-packed multi-values in seed:** `tests/unit/data_files.rs::seed_lino_values_never_pipe_pack_multi_values` fails on *any* `|` in a seed value except the exempt `code` field, so pipe packing can never silently return.

## Review response (canonical cache)
Addresses https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/399#issuecomment-4652626289:
- No `at-NNNN` generated array ids or scalar `string` tags remain in `data/**/*.lino`.
- Wikidata raw JSON lives beside compact LiNo in typed folders, and tests assert each LiNo projection is regenerated from the raw JSON snapshot.
- `links_notation::parse_lino(content.trim())` now validates data files without comment-stripping.
- `key: # ...` comment-only seed declarations and blank LiNo lines were removed.
- Recursive closure coverage walks bare Q/L/P ids found in seed/source and cache records, requiring checked-in `.json`/`.lino` for every reachable id.

## CI follow-up
Run https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/runs/27166268807 failed only on `windows-latest` because Git checked `.lino` files out as CRLF, while `json_cache_file()` emits LF. Commit `b1e1bc60` adds `.gitattributes` so Windows checks out LiNo/cache snapshots with LF and the canonical equality test compares the intended bytes.

## Review response (empty-redefinition fields, overrides layer, whole-tree CI)
Addresses https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/399#issuecomment-4663407299. Standards are recorded in `REQUIREMENTS.md` (R278-R283) under the governance rule **latest requirement overrides any earlier one**, each CI check mapped to a requirement.

**Defect 1 — empty-redefinition fields (resolved, R278).** Every `facet <kind>` wrapper whose child was an empty colon redefinition (`word_surface:`, `lexical_sense:`, …) is collapsed into the native Links Notation `subject predicate` form (`notation word_surface`, `denotation lexical_sense`) across the whole `data/seed` tree by the re-runnable `scripts/migrate-empty-facet-fields.rs`, which also regenerates the browser worker embed. `src/seed/meanings.rs` now reads both forms and de-duplicates targets. The previously-narrow guard is broadened: the tree-walking `seed_lino_files_have_no_empty_redefinition_fields` (`tests/unit/data_files.rs`) fails on any empty-bodied colon field with no deeper-indented child, with no hard-coded filename. Zero remain.

**New requirement — `data/overrides/` layer (resolved, R279).** A grounding override layer now sits beside `data/cache/` with the same per-id structure (`data/overrides/wikidata/{entity,property,lexeme}/<id>.lino`). Resolution is `(cache or live API) then overrides`: `formal_ai::seed::resolve` decorates a cached record with an override's facts (override wins on conflict, missing keys appended, untouched sections preserved). Each override records **why** it exists in a `reason "..."` line. The tree-walking `tests/unit/overrides.rs` fails when an override references an id with no checked-in cache record, omits its reason, carries no facts, or is **redundant** — repeating a value the cache already holds — so overrides shrink to zero as upstream catches up (CI check #6). The seeded example supplies the Hindi (`hi`) label Wikidata is missing for the KISS principle (Q131560).

**Whole-tree sweep + migration-first (resolved, R280/R281).** Both new guards walk their entire trees and assert on relative paths; both mutations are reproducible by algorithm rather than hand-edited (CI checks #1, #6, #7).

**Grounding floor (partial, R282).** Source-grounded meanings carry `grounded-in <Qid>` links whose recursive closure is verified against checked-in cache records. Grounding every remaining meaning to an external source — and sourcing per-language surfaces from those records instead of hand-typing them (CI checks #2, #3) — is a corpus-import effort larger than one PR and remains the primary follow-up; the grounding-floor CI check is held back until the data is grounded so it protects an invariant rather than only reddening CI. The override layer is the sanctioned interim way to record a source gap. Tracked in `docs/case-studies/issue-398/README.md`. The underscore→hyphen slug rename (CI check #5) and long-lived-quote sweep (CI check #4) are likewise tracked there: both are tree-wide renames whose string references reach into Rust tests and the worker embed, and are staged separately to avoid a destabilizing single-PR rewrite.

## Review response (full reference closure + role/predicate reconciliation)
Addresses points #1 and #2 of https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/399#issuecomment-4668342875.

**Reconciled the "~96% undefined" measurement.** The audit recognized only colon-head `slug:` definitions and missed the *primary* nested-under-`meanings` definition form, undercounting definitions ~10×. The seed actually defines **478** meanings; `experiments/closure_audit.py` documents the measurement.

**#1 — full reference closure (the missing check, resolved).** Over genuine meaning-reference fields (`defined-by` + the four facets `notation`/`annotation`/`denotation`/`connotation`), **every** target resolves to a defined meaning — 0 dangling across all 35 `meanings*.lino` files. `tests/unit/data_files.rs::meaning_definition_references_resolve_to_defined_meanings` walks the whole lexicon and fails CI naming any reference that does not resolve (verified with a negative test). The flagged "core vocabulary" splits cleanly: `concept`/`relation`/`entity`/`action`/`noun`/`word_surface` **are** defined meanings; `number`/`phrase`/`greeting` were over-counts of `text "..."` surface strings (literal words), not meaning links.

**#2 — structural predicates vs meaning links (resolved).** The only undefined references in def-fields were **131 `role` predicate values**, previously undeclared. `data/seed/roles.lino` is now the single canonical registry of all **207** roles, each classified `kind meaning` (also a defined slug — 76) or `kind predicate` (role-only — 131). `scripts/generate-role-registry.py` regenerates it deterministically/idempotently; `every_role_value_is_declared_in_the_registry` and `role_registry_is_in_lockstep_with_usage` keep registry and usage in lockstep with correct kind classification.

- **#3** reverse-dictionary / part-of-speech-as-meaning (the genuine residue: `verb`, `noun_phrase` used as POS tags but not yet defined meanings).

- **#5** provable 1:1 meaning↔type via relative-meta-logic.
- **#6** minimal seed + on-demand expansion.


## Review response (total closure + multi-source view)
Addresses https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/399#issuecomment-4668929105. Standards recorded in `REQUIREMENTS.md` (R284-R288), latest-overrides-earlier, each CI check mapped to a requirement.

**Total closure widened from the backbone to every token (R284).** The earlier gate only proved the structured `defined-by`/facet/role backbone closed. This round drives *every* non-keyword, non-quoted value token in `data/seed/**.lino` to resolution. `scripts/audit-total-closure.py` is the single-source resolver (a token resolves to a defined meaning in either syntax, a grounded `Q…/L…/P…`/Wiktionary/WordNet id with a checked-in cache record, a declared role, or a language code); its `--json` mode reports **0 unresolved over 1,410 distinct tokens** (1,003 defined meanings). `scripts/close-total.py` is the idempotent migration that closed the gap — it defines each previously-dangling internal token as a first-class meaning (17 parent category concepts rooted at `concept`, plus 508 members parented by the category their predicate implies) into `data/seed/closure-generated-{01,02}.lino`. The backbone `reference_closure.rs` gate stays as a stricter subset — both hold.

**WordNet (OEWN 2024) ingested (R285).** `scripts/ground-wordnet.py` imports Open English WordNet 2024 offline (one download via the `wn` library, no per-word network calls) and caches **312** English lemmas as `.json` + lossless `.lino` under `data/cache/wordnet/en/`, recorded under CC BY 4.0.

**`data/view/` multi-source merge layer (R286).** `scripts/build-views.py` merges the WordNet and Wiktionary caches into **536** per-lemma view entities, each with a deterministic `M-<sha1[:12]>` id (`view:<lang>:<lemma>` → identical id on every run), a sorted `sources` list, and per-sense `provenance`. Senses sharing part-of-speech with gloss content-word Jaccard ≥ 0.5 merge and keep both sources; otherwise they stay separate. `--check` reruns the build in memory to detect drift, reconfirms id determinism, asserts no provenance-less field, and runs the merge-threshold self-tests. **14** entities are genuinely multi-source on real data (both WordNet and Wiktionary).

**`sources-registry.lino` (R287).** `data/seed/sources-registry.lino` enumerates every ingested source (Wikidata, Wiktionary, WordNet, Wikipedia) with its API endpoint, permissive license, and cache path.

### CI gates added (`tests/unit/total_closure.rs`)
Six gates that fail immediately — and name offenders, never a bare count — if: any seed value token is unresolved; the seed collapses below hundreds of meanings / a full token surface; the WordNet cache is absent; `sources-registry.lino` omits an ingested source / API / license, or a populated cache dir is unregistered; `data/view/` is missing, drifted, non-deterministic, or has a provenance-less field; or no view entity is genuinely multi-source.

### Honesty notes
- Real lexicons phrase glosses differently, so at the 0.5 threshold there are **0 sense-level** merges on real data; the 14 multi-source entities merge at the **entity** level (same lemma, both sources). The sense-merge-threshold logic itself is verified by `build-views.py --selftest` with synthetic same/different pairs (same → merges, different → stays separate) plus id-determinism checks. This is stated plainly rather than presented as sense-level merging.
- Stopwords and abbreviations with no dictionary entry (`for`, `api`, `csv`, …) are closed by *defining* them as meanings via `close-total.py` — the reviewer-sanctioned "or it must be made one" fallback — not by claiming a grounding that does not exist.

All mass actions are preserved, re-runnable scripts (`audit-total-closure.py`, `ground-wordnet.py`, `ground-wiktionary.py`, `close-total.py`, `build-views.py`). Full `cargo test --test unit`: 814 passed, 1 ignored. `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` clean.

## Summary

Fixes #390.

This PR restores the GitHub release path after the repository reached a split state where crates.io and git tags advanced to `v0.177.0`, but GitHub Releases stopped at `v0.153.0`.

## Root Cause

- `scripts/create-github-release.rs` treated any GitHub API `Validation Failed` response as an idempotent duplicate release, so the CI/CD run for `0.177.0` printed `Release v0.177.0 already exists, skipping` even though `gh release view v0.177.0` returned not found.
- The `0.177.0` changelog section was 224,856 bytes, past the observed safe range for this repository's GitHub release body.
- The desktop `workflow_run` fallback selected the stale latest release (`v0.153.0`) instead of the release tag attached to the completed CI run SHA.
- Desktop packaging passed `--config package.json`, which made electron-builder treat the whole app manifest as a dedicated config object and reject the top-level `build` key.

## Changes

- Parse GitHub validation errors precisely and only skip exact duplicate release responses (`resource=Release`, `code=already_exists`, `field=tag_name`).
- Cap generated GitHub release bodies at 120,000 bytes and append a link to the tagged full `CHANGELOG.md`.
- Resolve desktop `workflow_run` builds from `github.event.workflow_run.head_sha`, verify the matching GitHub release exists, and skip instead of rebuilding a stale latest release.
- Remove `--config package.json` from desktop electron-builder invocations and add a smoke guard against reintroducing it.
- Add regression coverage for release body truncation, exact duplicate-release handling, generic validation failures, desktop tag resolution, and desktop builder config usage.
- Add the full issue case study and archived evidence: https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/issue-390-77cb1ef33735/docs/case-studies/issue-390/README.md

## Template Reports

- Rust template exact false-positive issue: https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/63

## How to reproduce / view it

```bash
# Serve the web app (which now includes /download) locally
bun run build:web && ./scripts/sync-seed.sh
npx serve src/web --listen 3456
# open http://localhost:3456/download/
```

The page auto-detects the visitor's OS, lists every cross-platform installer, fetches the latest release from the GitHub Releases API, verifies a downloaded artifact's SHA-256 **in the browser** against `SHA256SUMS.txt`, and honours the existing theme + locale switches (en / ru / zh / hi).
