## Summary

Fixes #72. The GitHub Pages demo at <https://link-assistant.github.io/formal-ai/> advertised `0.16.0` long after the crate moved past it because `src/web/index.html` carried a hardcoded version literal that no release step ever rewrote. This PR makes `Cargo.toml` the single source of truth for every user-facing version surface:

- **Web (`src/web/index.html`, `src/web/app.js`)** — the meta tag now uses a `__FORMAL_AI_VERSION__` placeholder (same convention as the existing `__FORMAL_AI_ASSET_VERSION__` cache-buster). The JS fallback no longer pins `0.16.0`; it shows `dev` when the placeholder is unreplaced so local Playwright runs stay sane.
- **Pages deploy (`scripts/stamp-pages-artifact.sh`, `.github/workflows/release.yml`)** — the stamp script accepts a 4th positional argument (or `FORMAL_AI_VERSION` env var), substitutes the placeholder, validates the rendered meta tag, and writes the rendered version into `deployment.json`. The `deploy-demo` job reads `Cargo.toml` with inline `sed` (no Rust setup needed) and forwards the value to the stamp script.
- **Live e2e wait (`scripts/wait-for-pages-deployment.sh`)** — now rejects both `__FORMAL_AI_ASSET_VERSION__` and `__FORMAL_AI_VERSION__` placeholders so a half-stamped deploy fails fast instead of going silently green.
- **CLI (`src/main.rs`)** — adds `version` to the clap `#[command(...)]` attribute. `formal-ai --version` prints `formal-ai <CARGO_PKG_VERSION>` via `lino-arguments`'s re-exported clap derive.
- **Telegram (`src/telegram.rs`)** — `reply_for_message` recognizes `/version` and `/version@formal_ai_bot` (case-insensitive) and replies with `formal-ai <CARGO_PKG_VERSION>` using `env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")`.

## Why one source of truth

Every surface now sources the version from cargo. clap exposes it via `version`, the Telegram bot reads `env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")` at compile time, and the Pages deploy reads `Cargo.toml` with `sed`. Because `cargo publish` and `scripts/version-and-commit.rs` both update `Cargo.toml`, every release path remains the single source of truth.

## Template comparison

The follow-up comment asked for the fix to be cross-checked against the four `link-foundation/{rust,js,python,csharp}-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template` repos. Each template's `release.yml` is captured under `docs/case-studies/issue-72/template-data/`:

- `rust-…-template` deploys `cargo doc` output — version comes from the build, no stale literal possible.
- `js-…-template`, `python-…-template`, `csharp-…-template` — no GitHub Pages deploy step at all.

The bug pattern (hardcoded version literal in a hand-written static site that the release pipeline never rewrites) only manifests in this repo because `formal-ai` ships a custom React demo. No upstream template issue is needed; the case study preserves the generalizable lesson for any future repo that adopts a similar custom-demo pattern.

## Case study

`docs/case-studies/issue-72/` collects the raw issue/PR JSON, the original deployment screenshot, every template's `release.yml`, and a README covering: requirements, root cause, end-to-end fix, regression coverage matrix, template comparison, online research, and the verification log.

- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test` — 224 unit + 76 framework + 8 integration tests pass; 69 pre-existing `#[ignore]`d MVP-target tests remain ignored.

Fixes #16

## Summary

This PR delivers the requirements from issue #16: every chat surface now answers in Russian, Hindi, and Chinese in addition to English; `What is X?` queries fall back to Wikipedia from the browser when the offline corpus does not cover the term; the deployable demo lives under `src/web/` next to the rest of the source tree; and the web UI persists every turn into an **append-only** memory log that can be exported and re-imported as Links Notation.

A second pass (R97-R100, requested in the first reopen comment) makes the demo fully data-driven: multilingual responses, the concept table, and the tool registry are all loaded from seeded `.lino` files; the UI surfaces the tool catalog with a `thinking` vs `agent` mode badge; every reasoning step and tool invocation is recorded in the append-only log; and a single **Download bundle** action exports the seed + memory + environment metadata as one Links Notation document that the `Report issue` link references.

A third pass (R101-R104, requested in the second reopen comment) generalises the seed loader so it is the canonical source for **every** interface — the Rust library, CLI, HTTP server, and Telegram webhook all `include_str!`-embed the same `data/seed/*.lino` files the browser worker fetches. The intent-routing rule book moves out of hardcoded match arms into `data/seed/intent-routing.lino` with explicit `keyword` / `phrase` / `token` / `combo` match semantics, and `seed::merged_bundle()` / `seed::parse_bundle()` (plus JS mirrors `FormalAiSeed.parseBundle` / `FormalAiSeed.loadFromBundle`) give the seed a complete single-file round-trip.

A fourth pass (R105-R108, requested in the third reopen comment) makes `data/seed/` the **only** tracked seed tree, makes the seed **self-aware of every environment** it ships in, and lets a user **migrate their agent's memory between any pair of surfaces** with a single `.lino` file. Each new requirement is wired through the library so every CLI capability is reachable from Rust code as well.

### Move `docs/demo/` → `src/web/`
- Commit `765b2ea` relocates the deployable artefact so it sits next to the other library/CLI/web sources.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` GitHub Pages deploy job already points at `src/web`.

### Multilingual surface (English, Russian, Hindi, Chinese)
- Rust: `src/language.rs` detects the input language from Unicode blocks (Cyrillic, Devanagari, CJK), `src/engine.rs::language_aware_answer_for` returns localized greetings/identity/unknown, and `src/concepts.rs` adds ru/hi/zh aliases plus a `What is X?` prefix/suffix matcher for all four languages.
- JS mirror: `src/web/formal_ai_worker.js` initialises mutable `MULTILINGUAL_ANSWERS`, `CONCEPTS`, and `TOOLS` tables from `data/seed/*.lino` (synced to `src/web/seed/` by `scripts/sync-seed.sh` and merged by `src/web/seed_loader.js`) instead of carrying hardcoded literals.

### Wikipedia REST fallback (`What is X?`)
- `src/web/formal_ai_worker.js` exposes `WIKIPEDIA_HOSTS`, `fetchWikipediaSummary`, and `tryWikipediaLookup`. The offline `CONCEPTS` table still wins whenever it can; the network call is reserved for out-of-corpus prompts.
- The handler is intentionally last in the synchronous-handler chain and returns a structured answer with `source:` evidence so the user can audit the citation. Falls back to the English host when the detected language has no article.

### Append-only memory log with export/import
- `src/web/memory.js`: IndexedDB-backed store. Public API exposes `appendEvent`, `listEvents`, `importEvents`, `exportLinksNotation`, `parseLinksNotation`, `exportBundle`, `formatEvent` — and **no** `delete`/`deleteEvent`/`forget`/`clear`/`remove` operation. Append-only is enforced by *omission* of any code path that could remove records.
- The event schema gains optional `kind`, `tool`, `inputs`, and `outputs` fields so reasoning steps and tool invocations can land in the same log without breaking older event shapes.
- `src/web/app.js` topbar adds **Export memory**, **Import memory**, and **Download bundle** buttons plus a status indicator. Export downloads `formal-ai-memory.lino`; Import accepts the same shape and never deletes existing events; bundle downloads `formal-ai-bundle.lino`.

### Data-driven configuration (R97-R100)
- **Seeded constants.** `data/seed/multilingual-responses.lino`, `data/seed/concepts.lino` (with multilingual `aliases`), and `data/seed/tools.lino` define the agent's responses, concept table, and tool registry. The web worker loads them at boot via `src/web/seed_loader.js` and merges them into mutable runtime tables; user-provided changes are layered on top by editing the seed.
- **Tool registry UI.** The context panel renders the loaded tools (`http_fetch`, `web_search`, `wikipedia_lookup`, `eval_js`, `read_local_file`, `append_memory`, `export_memory`) with a `thinking` vs `agent` mode badge. The worker dispatches `wikipedia_lookup`, `eval_js`, and `concept_lookup` end-to-end and records every invocation as a `kind:"tool_call"` event.
- **Reasoning + tool-call events.** `solve()` returns structured `steps[]` (`impulse`, `formalize`, `detect_language`, `match_rule`/`dispatch_handler`/`invoke_tool`, `fallback`) and `toolCalls[]`. `appendAssistantMessage` writes each one to the append-only log alongside the user/assistant turns.
- **Single-file reproducibility.** `FormalAiMemory.exportBundle({seed, events, info})` produces a `formal_ai_bundle` Links Notation document containing environment metadata, every seed file in full, and every recorded event. The prefilled **Report issue** body ends with an `Attach full state` section that asks the reporter to drag the bundle into the issue, so the maintainer can fully reconstruct the agent's state from a single attachment.

### Universal seed + bundle round-trip (R101-R104)
- **R101 — Universal seed loader.** `src/seed.rs` `include_str!`-embeds every `data/seed/*.lino` file and exposes typed accessors (`multilingual_responses_for`, `concept_records`, `tool_records`, `language_rule_records`, `prompt_pattern_records`, `intent_route_records`) plus `seed_files()` for the merged-bundle path. The Rust library, CLI binary, HTTP server, and Telegram webhook all read from these accessors so a single `data/seed/` edit reaches every surface; the browser worker continues to fetch the same files at runtime through `src/web/seed_loader.js`. `scripts/sync-seed.sh` keeps `src/web/seed/` mirrored from `data/seed/` for the GitHub Pages deploy.
- **R102 — REQUIREMENTS colocation.** `REQUIREMENTS.md` now sits next to `VISION.md` at the repository root so the architecture story and the requirement matrix are reviewed together. All cross-references (case studies, changelog fragments not yet released) were updated.
- **R103 — Intent routing as data.** `data/seed/intent-routing.lino` carries every routing rule with explicit match semantics: `keyword` (whole-prompt exact, case-insensitive), `phrase` (whole-prompt exact multi-word), `token` (single-token substring), and `combo` (all tokens present anywhere). The Rust handler dispatcher and the JS worker both parse this seed at boot and dispatch handlers from the data; previously hardcoded match arms are gone. A regression test (`hello_world_request_is_not_routed_to_greeting`) pins down the keyword/token split.
- **R104 — Single-file bundle round-trip.** `seed::merged_bundle()` produces a `formal_ai_seed_bundle` Links Notation document containing every seed file in full; `seed::parse_bundle()` walks the document and recovers the per-category split files. The JS side mirrors this with `FormalAiSeed.parseBundle()` / `FormalAiSeed.loadFromBundle()`, so a single `.lino` upload reconstitutes the agent's static knowledge surface without sacrificing the maintenance-friendly split.

### Self-aware environments + cross-surface memory migration (R105-R108)
- **R105 — Single tracked seed tree.** `src/web/seed/` is now a generated deployment mirror (added to `.gitignore`); the tracked copies were deleted and `scripts/sync-seed.sh` is invoked from CI before the e2e job and the GitHub Pages upload so the browser still has the same `.lino` files at runtime. `data/seed/` is the only source of truth.
- **R106 — Self-aware environments.** `data/seed/environments.lino` declares every interface the agent ships in (`browser`, `rust_library`, `cli`, `http_server`, `telegram`, `docker_microservice`) plus the cross-surface migration flows (`browser_to_cli`, `cli_to_browser`, `browser_to_browser`, `cli_to_cli`). `src/seed.rs` exposes typed accessors (`environment_directory`, `environment_records`, `EnvironmentRecord`, `MigrationFlow`) and the new `formal-ai environments` CLI command renders the directory so a user can list every surface and the documented portability flows from any one of them.
- **R107 — Cross-surface memory migration.** `src/memory.rs` introduces a portable `MemoryStore` / `MemoryEvent` model that round-trips through the same `demo_memory` Links Notation format the browser writes to IndexedDB. `formal-ai memory export|import|show` and `formal-ai bundle export|import` give the CLI parity with the browser's `Export memory` / `Import memory` / `Download bundle` buttons, and `--path -` selects stdin/stdout so `formal-ai memory export --from … --path - | ssh host formal-ai memory import --path -` works without temp files. Library users get the same capability via `export_memory_links_notation`, `parse_memory_links_notation`, `export_memory_bundle`, and `extract_memory_from_bundle`.
- **R108 — Library-first availability.** Every CLI capability is also re-exported from `src/lib.rs` (engine, protocol, seed accessors, environment directory, memory primitives), so a downstream Rust crate can embed `formal-ai` and reach the same answers, the same intent routes, the same environment directory, and the same import/export pipeline without shelling out to the binary. A new `environment_records_match_directory` test pins library/CLI parity.

### Playwright e2e (local + GitHub Pages)
- `tests/e2e/tests/multilingual.spec.js` — 14 tests covering:
  - Russian/Hindi greetings replying in the same language
  - Chinese identity prompt (`你是谁?`) replying in Chinese
  - Russian/Chinese `What is X?` resolving from the offline `CONCEPTS` table
  - Wikipedia REST fallback for `What is Albert Einstein?` (stubbed via `page.route` so the test is hermetic)
  - Export/Import buttons present + producing a `.lino` file with `demo_memory`/`role`/`content`
  - Assertion that `window.FormalAiMemory` exposes no delete/forget/clear API
  - `Download bundle` produces a `formal_ai_bundle` file with seed and memory log
  - `Report issue` link references the bundle in the prefilled body
  - Tool registry surfaces seed-loaded tools with mode badges
  - Reasoning steps and tool calls land in the append-only log
- Both `tests/e2e/playwright.local.config.js` (PR runs against `npx serve src/web` after `scripts/sync-seed.sh`) and `tests/e2e/playwright.pages.config.js` (post-deploy run against the live `link-assistant.github.io/formal-ai`) match `**/multilingual.spec.js`.

### Documentation

## Summary
- Replaced the demo deploy job's `peaceiris/actions-gh-pages` branch push with the official GitHub Pages artifact deployment flow: `configure-pages`, `upload-pages-artifact`, and `deploy-pages`.
- Exposed the Pages deployment URL from the deploy job and made the GitHub Pages e2e job test that exact deployed URL.
- Added workflow regression tests so the release workflow cannot silently return to `gh-pages` branch publishing for a workflow-sourced Pages site.
- Added a case study with preserved logs/raw data and a template comparison across JS, Rust, Python, and C# pipeline templates.
- Added CI/CD troubleshooting docs for the “deploy succeeded but Pages did not update” failure mode.

## Reproduction and Root Cause
The failed run `25746871509` reported a successful `Deploy Demo to GitHub Pages` job while the later `E2E Tests (GitHub Pages)` job failed against `https://link-assistant.github.io/formal-ai` with 14 failures. The preserved repo Pages settings show `build_type: workflow`, but the old workflow only pushed `docs/demo` to the `gh-pages` branch. That branch push can succeed without creating or serving a Pages deployment for a workflow-sourced Pages site, which produced the false-positive deploy job.

Full investigation and raw evidence are in `docs/case-studies/issue-4/README.md`.

## Template Follow-up
The JS template already uses the official Pages artifact flow. The Rust template still has the same risky `peaceiris/actions-gh-pages` pattern for docs, so I filed an upstream template issue: https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/48
